knowledge_statements.title: Optimized Halpern Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon minimax representation of optimized Halpern coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty bounded closed convex subset of a Hilbert space \(H\), let \(u,x_0\in C\), let \(N\ge1\), and let \(\mathcal T\) be a nonempty prescribed class of nonexpansive maps \(T:C\to C\). For each \(\alpha=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{N-1})\in[0,1]^N\) and \(T\in\mathcal T\), generate
\[
x_{k+1}=\alpha_ku+(1-\alpha_k)Tx_k\qquad(0\le k<N)
\]
and define
\[
\mathcal R_N(\alpha)=\sup_{T\in\mathcal T}\|x_N-Tx_N\|.
\]
A finite-horizon optimized Halpern coefficient vector is any
\[
\alpha^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in[0,1]^N}\mathcal R_N(\alpha).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed bounded class of nonexpansive self-maps and a fixed horizon, optimized Halpern coefficients minimize the worst-case terminal fixed-point residual over all coefficient vectors in the unit cube.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty bounded closed convex subset of a Hilbert space \(H\).
\(\mathcal T\) is a nonempty prescribed class of nonexpansive maps \(T:C\to C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in[0,1]^N}\mathcal R_N(\alpha)\).

children.title: Parameter-Free Halpern Families

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\) has \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
The method may observe iterates, residuals, and completed oracle evaluations, but receives no conditioning constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining requirement is \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)Tx_k\), where every \(\alpha_k\) and any auxiliary accepted step are determined without unknown Lipschitz, cocoercivity, strong-monotonicity, or error-bound constants.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: parameter-free denotes independence from unavailable conditioning constants
exact admissible parameter-free family and residual guarantee require a dedicated source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines parameter freedom operationally; it does not assert a convergence rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Halpern family is parameter-free relative to a declared oracle when it generates \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)Tx_k\) and selects \(\alpha_k\), stopping times, and any auxiliary trial steps using only iteration indices and previously observed oracle data. In particular, its rules cannot depend on unavailable constants such as a Lipschitz bound \(L\), cocoercivity constant \(\beta\), strong-monotonicity modulus \(\mu\), or error-bound constant \(\kappa\). Any safeguards must be checkable from computed quantities and must terminate before the accepted update is formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameter-free Halpern scheme chooses all weights and safeguards from observed data, without unavailable conditioning constants.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Free Halpern Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The operational distinction is plausible, but the exact oracle-relative meaning of parameter-free and the asserted safeguard requirements need a dedicated, inspectable source.

children.title: Adaptive Halpern Families
children.top_down_role: Halpern schemes whose controls respond to observed iteration behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(u,x_0\in H\), and \(T:H\to H\) has a nonempty fixed-point set.
Each weight is chosen from information available before the corresponding update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the accepted weights satisfy \(0<\alpha_k<1\), \(\alpha_k\to0\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\), the resulting recursion belongs to the adaptive Halpern family.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: adaptive Halpern weights are history-measurable and satisfy classical admissibility conditions
specific adaptation rules and convergence hypotheses require a dedicated source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract history-dependent Halpern wrapper, without committing to one line-search rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in H\). At iteration \(k\), form the history \(\mathcal F_k=\sigma(x_0,Tx_0,\ldots,x_k,Tx_k)\), choose an \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable weight \(\alpha_k\in(0,1)\), and update \[x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)Tx_k.\] The family is admissible when its realized weights obey \(\alpha_k\to0\) and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\); a concrete adaptive member must additionally specify a computable selection rule and any safeguards. Stop when a prescribed test on \(\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert\) is met, and return \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive Halpern methods choose each anchoring weight from the observed iteration history while retaining the standard vanishing, nonsummable weight conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Halpern Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but the stated weight conditions are not by themselves a universal Halpern convergence hypothesis. A source must establish the intended adaptive family and any additional regularity conditions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information classification for comparing anchored algorithms, independent of their convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be the conditioning quantities relevant to a problem class. The full-information regime supplies \(\mathcal K=\mathcal C\) before iteration; the partial-information regime supplies a strict subset \(\mathcal K\subsetneq\mathcal C\); the unknown-conditioning regime has \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\). A method is conditioning-free relative to \(\mathcal C\) when its updates, acceptance tests, and stopping rule depend only on oracle outputs and declared nonconditioning data. It is adaptively conditioned when it constructs estimates \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_k\) from observed data and bases subsequent choices on those estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditioning-information regimes distinguish constants known initially, partly known, wholly unknown, or estimated online from oracle observations.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning-Information Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The information-regime classification is coherent, but its terminology and the precise distinction between conditioning-free and adaptive estimation are source-dependent.

children.title: Residual-to-Inclusion Certificate Conversion
children.top_down_role: Conversion of fixed-point residuals to problem-class certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Inclusion Certificate Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conversion for a resolvent residual and the inclusion \(0\in Ay\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone, let \(\gamma>0\), and let \(y=J_{\gamma A}x\). Define \[v=\frac{x-y}{\gamma}.\] Then \(v\in Ay\) and \[\lVert v\rVert=\frac{1}{\gamma}\lVert x-J_{\gamma A}x\rVert.\] In particular, \(\lVert x-J_{\gamma A}x\rVert\leq\gamma\varepsilon\) gives the inclusion certificate \(v\in Ay\) with \(\lVert v\rVert\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a resolvent point, dividing the fixed-point residual by the positive stepsize produces an operator value; a residual at most gamma times epsilon therefore gives an inclusion certificate of norm at most epsilon.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computable pair \((y,v)\), with \(v=(x-y)/\gamma\), satisfies \(v\in Ay\) and \(\lVert v\rVert=\lVert x-J_{\gamma A}x\rVert/\gamma\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the resolvent identity converts a fixed-point residual into a graph point

children.title: Halpern-Type Splitting Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Anchored adaptations of the principal resolvent and corrected-forward families.

children.title: Halpern-Type Proximal Point Methods
children.top_down_role: Anchored resolvent iteration.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update is an anchored resolvent step, and \(\operatorname{Fix}J_{\gamma_k A}=\operatorname{zer}A\) for every \(\gamma_k>0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: applying the Halpern wrapper to a resolvent gives the anchored proximal-point method
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic anchored proximal-point scheme; convergence requires additional control of weights and stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in H\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute the proximal point \(p_k=J_{\gamma_k A}x_k\) and set \[x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)p_k.\] Equivalently, choose \(a_k=(x_k-p_k)/\gamma_k\in Ap_k\) and anchor the next iterate between \(u\) and \(p_k\). Stop when \(\lVert x_k-p_k\rVert/\gamma_k\leq\varepsilon\), returning \(p_k\) together with \(a_k\); otherwise continue. For every positive stepsize, the target identity is \(\operatorname{Fix}J_{\gamma_k A}=\operatorname{zer}A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Halpern proximal-point method convexly combines a fixed anchor with each resolvent evaluation and can return an explicit inclusion residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Halpern-Type Proximal Point Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The anchored resolvent algorithm and fixed-point identity are mathematically standard and fit the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports the Halpern-type proximal formulation.

children.title: Halpern-Type Forward–Backward Methods
children.top_down_role: Anchored explicit-implicit splitting.

assumptions_latex: \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone and \(B:H\to H\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update is Halpern iteration for \(T_\gamma=J_{\gamma A}(I-\gamma B)\), whose fixed points are exactly \(\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: forward–backward splitting is an averaged fixed-point map under the cocoercive stepsize bound
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-stepsize anchored forward–backward splitting for a cocoercive forward term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(u,x_0\in H\), define \(T_\gamma=J_{\gamma A}(I-\gamma B)\). At iteration \(k\), evaluate \(b_k=Bx_k\), compute \(p_k=J_{\gamma A}(x_k-\gamma b_k)\), and update \[x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)p_k.\] Stop when \(\lVert x_k-p_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\), returning \(x_k\) or the resolvent point \(p_k\) according to the certificate convention. The identities \(p_k=T_\gamma x_k\) and \(\operatorname{Fix}T_\gamma=\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\) connect the splitting residual to the target inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anchored forward–backward splitting applies one explicit cocoercive step, one resolvent step, and then a Halpern convex combination.
knowledge_statements.title: Halpern-Type Forward–Backward Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward–backward map and fixed-point identity are correct under the stated cocoercive stepsize bound. A source is still required for the anchored algorithm, and the stopping output must ultimately be tied to a precise certificate convention.

children.title: Anchored Extragradient Variants
children.top_down_role: Anchored corrected-forward schemes based on extragradient constructions.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(F:C\to H\) is monotone and \(L\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two projected forward evaluations define an anchored extragradient member targeting \(0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: metric projection onto the constraint set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: extragradient uses a projected prediction followed by correction at the predicted point
placement of Halpern anchoring varies across published variants and needs a dedicated source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected anchored extragradient template for monotone Lipschitz variational inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in C\). For each \(k\), form the prediction \[y_k=P_C(x_k-\gamma Fx_k),\] then the corrected point \[z_k=P_C(x_k-\gamma Fy_k),\] and apply Halpern anchoring by \[x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)z_k.\] A residual-based implementation stops when a declared computable test, such as \(\lVert x_k-y_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\), is met and returns the associated point. This template uses two evaluations of \(F\) per iteration and targets solutions of \(0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anchored extragradient predicts with one projected forward step, corrects using the predicted operator value, and anchors the corrected point.
knowledge_statements.title: Anchored Extragradient Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a plausible anchored Korpelevich template, but anchoring placement and the meaning of the proposed residual test vary across variants and require a specific source.

children.title: Anchored Popov Variants
children.top_down_role: Anchored corrected-forward schemes based on Popov constructions.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(F:C\to H\) is monotone and Lipschitz.
The stepsize and anchoring weights satisfy the safeguards required by the selected Popov variant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursion uses one new evaluation of \(F\) per iteration after initialization while retaining a Halpern anchor.

notation.meaning: metric projection onto the constraint set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Popov-type schemes reuse a stored operator value to reduce new evaluations
exact anchored Popov recursion and admissible stepsize vary by source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-oracle-call anchored Popov template; exact convergence conditions remain source-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0,y_{-1}\in C\) and store \(Fy_{-1}\). For iteration \(k\), compute \[y_k=P_C(x_k-\gamma Fy_{k-1}),\] evaluate the single new value \(Fy_k\), form \[z_k=P_C(x_k-\gamma Fy_k),\] and set \[x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)z_k.\] Stop under a prescribed residual test and return the tested point. The stored value \(Fy_k\) is reused at the next iteration, so after initialization the recursion makes one new evaluation of \(F\) per step, although it performs two projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An anchored Popov scheme reuses the preceding operator value, requiring one new operator evaluation per iteration before applying the anchor.
knowledge_statements.title: Anchored Popov Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-new-evaluation accounting is internally consistent, but the displayed anchored Popov recursion and its admissible stepsize and weight safeguards are source-dependent.

children.title: Corrected-Forward Interface
children.top_down_role: Shared operator-splitting structure behind the two anchored families.

assumptions_latex: \(G:H\to H\) is a single-valued forward oracle and \(C_\gamma:H\times H\times H\to H\) is a computable correction map.
The induced map has fixed points equal to the target solution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any corrected-forward map \(T_\gamma x=C_\gamma(x,Gx,G(P_\gamma(x,Gx)))\) can be wrapped by \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)T_\gamma x_k\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: corrected-forward methods expose an induced fixed-point map to an outer anchoring wrapper
the intended predictor-corrector interface is taxonomy-specific and needs a dedicated source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract interface separating a corrected-forward inner map from Halpern anchoring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A corrected-forward interface consists of a predictor \(p=P_\gamma(x,Gx)\), a new oracle value \(Gp\), and a correction \(T_\gamma x=C_\gamma(x,Gx,Gp)\). It is compatible with Halpern anchoring when \(T_\gamma:H\to H\) is everywhere defined, its fixed points coincide with the target solutions, and its regularity is sufficient for the chosen Halpern theorem. The outer method is then represented by \[x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)T_\gamma x_k.\] Extragradient and Popov constructions differ through \(P_\gamma\), \(C_\gamma\), and the oracle values retained between iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The corrected-forward interface packages prediction and correction as one fixed-point map, which an outer Halpern step can anchor.
knowledge_statements.title: Corrected-Forward Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the interface leaf, but \(P_\gamma\) is not formally typed and “regularity sufficient for the chosen Halpern theorem” is not an explicit condition. The intended interface needs a dedicated source before its exact formulation can be fixed.

children.title: Halpern-Type Douglas–Rachford Methods
children.top_down_role: Anchored reflected-resolvent splitting.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is Halpern anchoring of \(T_{\mathrm{DR}}=\tfrac12(I+R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A})\); its shadow variables provide a computable splitting certificate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Douglas–Rachford is a reflected-resolvent fixed-point map admitting a Halpern wrapper
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anchored Douglas–Rachford iteration with primal shadow and graph residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in H\). At iteration \(k\), compute \[p_k=J_{\gamma A}x_k,\qquad q_k=J_{\gamma B}(2p_k-x_k),\qquad z_k=x_k+q_k-p_k,\] and update \[x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)z_k.\] Here \(z_k=T_{\mathrm{DR}}x_k\), where \(T_{\mathrm{DR}}=\tfrac12(I+R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A})\). Stop when \(\lVert p_k-q_k\rVert/\gamma\leq\varepsilon\). The graph elements \(a_k=(x_k-p_k)/\gamma\in Ap_k\) and \(b_k=(2p_k-x_k-q_k)/\gamma\in Bq_k\) satisfy \(a_k+b_k=(p_k-q_k)/\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Halpern Douglas–Rachford anchors the reflected-resolvent update; its two shadow points yield a computable graph residual for the inclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Halpern-Type Douglas–Rachford Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Douglas–Rachford formulas and graph-element identity are correct and the algorithm kind fits. An inspectable source is required for the anchored variant and for treating the two-point shadow residual as the declared splitting certificate.

children.title: Anchored Fixed-Point Families
children.top_down_role: Fixed-point families organized around an explicit anchor.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural property of the constant-weight member of an anchored nonexpansive family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive, fix \(u\in H\), and choose \(0<\alpha\leq1\). The anchored mapping \[S_\alpha x=\alpha u+(1-\alpha)Tx\] is a contraction with modulus \(1-\alpha\). Consequently, it has a unique fixed point \(z_\alpha\), characterized by \[z_\alpha=\alpha u+(1-\alpha)Tz_\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed positive anchoring weight, the anchored map is contractive and has a unique regularized fixed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_\alpha\) is \((1-\alpha)\)-contractive and has a unique fixed point \(z_\alpha\).

notation.meaning: unique fixed point of the anchored mapping

knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Weight Anchored Map Is Contractive

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(T:H\to H\), and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every update \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)Tx_k\) lies on the segment joining the anchor \(u\) to the current image \(Tx_k\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: anchored fixed-point iteration is defined by convexly combining a fixed anchor with the operator image
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Umbrella definition for fixed-operator Halpern families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An anchored fixed-point family for \(T\) and anchor \(u\) consists of sequences generated from \(x_0\in H\) by \[x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)Tx_k,\qquad \alpha_k\in[0,1].\] The anchor remains fixed throughout the run, while the weight schedule may be predetermined or selected from past information. The associated fixed-point residual is \(r_k=x_k-Tx_k\). A concrete member of the family must state its weight rule, oracle used to evaluate \(T\), stopping criterion, and assumptions under which its iterates or residuals converge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An anchored fixed-point method repeatedly combines a fixed anchor with the current operator image using a possibly varying convex weight.
knowledge_statements.title: Anchored Fixed-Point Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is precise, internally consistent, and correctly placed, but it has no citation with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Halpern–Anchoring Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural links between classical Halpern schemes and broader anchoring mechanisms.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(T:H\to H\), and \(u,x_k\in H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Halpern update and anchored residual correction are identical: \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)Tx_k=x_k-[(1-\alpha_k)(I-T)x_k+\alpha_k(x_k-u)]\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct algebra identifies Halpern averaging with an anchored residual-correction step
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic correspondence, without adding convergence assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x_k,u\in H\) and \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\), the Halpern convex-combination form has the equivalent anchored correction form \[\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)Tx_k=x_k-\bigl((1-\alpha_k)(I-T)x_k+\alpha_k(x_k-u)\bigr).\] Thus the usual fixed-point correction \((I-T)x_k\) is scaled by \(1-\alpha_k\), while \(\alpha_k(x_k-u)\) pulls the iterate toward the fixed anchor. Conversely, any update with the displayed two correction terms expands uniquely to the Halpern form with the same \(T\), \(u\), and \(\alpha_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Halpern averaging is exactly a fixed-point residual step plus a weighted correction pulling the iterate toward the anchor.
knowledge_statements.title: Halpern–Anchoring Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic correspondence is correct, the representation kind fits the leaf, and the plain and LaTeX statements agree. It nevertheless lacks an inspectable citation.

children.title: Fixed-Point Residuals
children.top_down_role: Displacement-based fixed-point certificates.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\) is single-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_T(x)=0\iff x\in\operatorname{Fix}T\).

notation.meaning: Fixed-point residual at the candidate point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Displacement certificate for a single-valued fixed-point formulation on a Hilbert space.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.4 Fixed-point theorems p. 141
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) and define the fixed-point residual by \(r_T(x):=x-Tx\). Its norm \(\|r_T(x)\|\) is an exactly computable certificate of fixed-point feasibility: \[\|r_T(x)\|=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=Tx\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname{Fix}T.\] Consequently, \(\|r_T(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies that the displacement of \(x\) under \(T\) is at most \(\varepsilon\); this statement alone does not bound the distance from \(x\) to \(\operatorname{Fix}T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The displacement between a point and its image is zero exactly at fixed points; a small displacement is a directly verifiable residual certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Residuals

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1.4 Fixed-point theorems p. 141
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. I

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Point Residual Need Not Control Global Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a global residual error bound for a nonexpansive self-map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(H=\mathbb R\), let \(T(x)=x-\arctan x\). Then \(0\leq T'(x)<1\), so \(T\) is nonexpansive, and \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\{0\}\). Nevertheless, \[|x-Tx|=|\arctan x|\leq\frac\pi2,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{Fix}T)=|x|\to\infty.\] Thus no finite global \(\kappa\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{Fix}T)\leq\kappa\|x-Tx\|\) for all \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonexpansive map can have bounded displacement while distance to its fixed point is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nexists\,\kappa<\infty\ \forall x:\ |x|\leq\kappa|x-Tx|.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Residual Need Not Control Global Distance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz and firm-nonexpansiveness properties of the displacement residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R=I-T\), if \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive, then \[\|Rx-Ry\|\leq2\|x-y\|.\] If \(T\) is firmly nonexpansive, then \(R\) is firmly nonexpansive: \[\|Rx-Ry\|^2\leq\langle Rx-Ry,x-y\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The displacement of a nonexpansive map is two-Lipschitz, and the displacement of a firmly nonexpansive map is firmly nonexpansive.
assumptions_latex: \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive; the second conclusion additionally assumes firm nonexpansiveness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I-T\text{ is }2\text{-Lipschitz, and is firmly nonexpansive when }T\text{ is firmly nonexpansive}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Regularity of the Fixed-Point Displacement

children.title: Natural Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual certificates adapted to constrained monotone inclusions.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(F:H\to H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_\lambda(x)=0\iff 0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: Metric projection onto the feasible set.
Convex-analytic normal cone to the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-based residual for a variational inequality over a closed convex set.

source_refs.locator: Chapter III. Variational Inequalities for Monotone Operators p. 83
source_refs.source_title: An Introduction to Variational Inequalities and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(R_\lambda(x):=x-P_C(x-\lambda F(x))\). The metric-projection characterization gives the exact representation \[R_\lambda(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=P_C(x-\lambda F(x))\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in F(x)+N_C(x).\] Equivalently, vanishing of the natural residual characterizes solutions of the variational inequality \(\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\) for every \(y\in C\). Thus \(\|R_\lambda(x)\|\) is a computable fixed-point representation of inclusion feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The natural residual is the displacement from a projected forward step, and it vanishes exactly at solutions of the associated variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Natural Residuals

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter III. Variational Inequalities for Monotone Operators p. 83
source_witnesses.source_title: An Introduction to Variational Inequalities and Their Applications

children.title: Forward–Backward Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual certificates adapted to composite forward–backward structure.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(A:H\to H\) is single-valued, and \(B:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_\lambda(x)=0\iff 0\in A(x)+B(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent residual for the composite monotone inclusion \(0\in A+B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y:=J_{\lambda B}(x-\lambda A(x))\) and define \(G_\lambda(x):=(x-y)/\lambda\). The resolvent relation is \[G_\lambda(x)-A(x)\in B(y).\] Hence \[G_\lambda(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y=x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad -A(x)\in B(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in A(x)+B(x).\] Therefore \(\|G_\lambda(x)\|\) is an exact zero certificate for the forward-backward fixed-point formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward-backward residual is the scaled displacement of a resolvent step and vanishes exactly when the composite inclusion holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Forward–Backward Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward–backward residual formula and zero equivalence appear correct, but the record supplies no evidence source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Residual-Conversion Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Comparability and transfer between natural and forward–backward certificates.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(A:H\to H\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz, and \(B:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v:=G_\lambda(x)+A(y)-A(x)\in(A+B)(y)\) and \(\|v\|\leq(1+\lambda L)\|G_\lambda(x)\|\).

notation.meaning: Forward-backward residual at the input point.
Inclusion residual at the updated point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion from a forward-backward displacement to an inclusion residual at the updated point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The resolvent identity yields \(G_\lambda(x)-A(x)\in B(y)\). Consequently, the vector \[v:=G_\lambda(x)+A(y)-A(x)\] satisfies \(v\in A(y)+B(y)\). Lipschitz continuity of \(A\) and the identity \(x-y=\lambda G_\lambda(x)\) give \[\|v\|\leq\|G_\lambda(x)\|+L\|y-x\|=(1+\lambda L)\|G_\lambda(x)\|.\] Thus a forward-backward residual at \(x\) converts into a controlled inclusion residual at \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward-backward residual produces an explicit inclusion residual at the updated point, with a norm bound determined by the stepsize and Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Conversion Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated conversion and norm bound appear correct, but they are unsupported by a citation and the statement includes derivational proof text that should be removed after sourcing.

children.title: Enlargement Certificates
children.top_down_role: Approximate graph-membership certificates expressed through operator enlargements.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex aggregation for a maximally monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be maximally monotone, \(v_i\in T^{[\varepsilon_i]}(x_i)\), and \(\theta_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_i\theta_i=1\). Set \(\bar x=\sum_i\theta_i x_i\), \(\bar v=\sum_i\theta_i v_i\), and \(\bar\varepsilon=\sum_i\theta_i(\varepsilon_i+\langle x_i-\bar x,v_i-\bar v\rangle)\). Then \(\bar\varepsilon\ge0\) and \(\bar v\in T^{[\bar\varepsilon]}(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a maximally monotone operator, convex averages of enlargement-certified pairs remain certified with an explicit transported tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar\varepsilon\ge0\) and \(\bar v\in T^{[\bar\varepsilon]}(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Transportation Formula for Enlargement Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Tolerance Is Not Exact without Maximality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exact graph recovery for a nonmaximal monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\mathbb R\) and \(\operatorname{gra}T=\{(0,0)\}\). Then \(T\) is monotone but not maximally monotone, and \(T^{[0]}(0)=\mathbb R\supsetneq T(0)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonmaximal monotone graph, zero enlargement tolerance can admit vectors outside the graph.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Tolerance Is Not Exact without Maximality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Convex Values and Tolerance Nesting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic order and convexity structure of enlargement certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every monotone \(T\), each value \(T^{[\varepsilon]}(x)\) is a possibly empty closed convex subset of \(H\). Moreover, if \(0\le\varepsilon_1\le\varepsilon_2\), then \(T^{[\varepsilon_1]}(x)\subseteq T^{[\varepsilon_2]}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlargement values are closed and convex, and they grow with the allowed monotonicity defect.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T^{[\varepsilon]}(x)\) is closed and convex, and \(T^{[\varepsilon_1]}(x)\subseteq T^{[\varepsilon_2]}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex Values and Tolerance Nesting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar equivalent of the epsilon-enlargement predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F_T(x,v)=\sup_{(y,u)\in\operatorname{gra}T}(\langle x,u\rangle+\langle y,v\rangle-\langle y,u\rangle)\). For every \(\varepsilon\ge0\), \(v\in T^{[\varepsilon]}(x)\) if and only if \(F_T(x,v)\le\langle x,v\rangle+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlargement membership is equivalent to a Fitzpatrick-function inequality with additive tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\in T^{[\varepsilon]}(x)\iff F_T(x,v)-\langle x,v\rangle\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fitzpatrick Representation of Enlargement Membership

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\rightrightarrows H\) is monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\in T^{[\varepsilon]}(x)\), with \(T^{[0]}=T\) when \(T\) is maximally monotone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate graph membership through the standard epsilon-enlargement of a monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((x,v)\) carries an enlargement certificate of tolerance \(\varepsilon\) when \[v\in T^{[\varepsilon]}(x):=\left\{w\in H:\langle x-y,w-u\rangle\geq-\varepsilon\ \text{for every }(y,u)\in\operatorname{gra}T\right\}.\] This predicate is directly verifiable against the graph and relaxes monotonicity-compatible graph membership. If \(T\) is maximally monotone, then \(T^{[0]}=T\), so a zero-tolerance enlargement certificate is exactly the assertion \((x,v)\in\operatorname{gra}T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An enlargement certificate relaxes graph membership by allowing a uniform monotonicity defect of at most epsilon against every graph point.
knowledge_statements.title: Enlargement Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The enlargement definition and the maximal-monotonicity zero-tolerance claim are standard, but no authoritative source or locator is provided.

children.title: Inexact-Proximal Certificates
children.top_down_role: Approximate graph-membership certificates arising from inexact proximal evaluations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative enlargement-plus-resolvent error criterion used by hybrid proximal-extragradient steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For input \(x\), parameter \(\lambda>0\), and \(0\leq\sigma<1\), a tuple \((y,v,\varepsilon)\) is a relative-error inexact-proximal certificate when \[v\in T^{[\varepsilon]}(y),\qquad \|\lambda v+y-x\|^2+2\lambda\varepsilon\leq\sigma^2\|y-x\|^2.\] For \(\sigma=0\), the certificate forces \(\varepsilon=0\) and \(\lambda v+y-x=0\), hence gives an exact proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative inexact-proximal certificate jointly controls enlargement error and resolvent-equation error by the step displacement.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\in T^{[\varepsilon]}(y)\) and \(\|\lambda v+y-x\|^2+2\lambda\varepsilon\leq\sigma^2\|y-x\|^2\) certify a relative-error proximal step.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Error Inexact-Proximal Certificate

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(T:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone, and \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\in T^{[\varepsilon]}(y)\) and \(\lambda v+y-x=e\) certify an inexact proximal step.

notation.meaning: Input point and reported proximal point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-error certificate for an approximate resolvent evaluation using operator enlargement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tuple \((y,v,\varepsilon,e)\) is an inexact-proximal certificate for input \(x\) and parameter \(\lambda\) when \[v\in T^{[\varepsilon]}(y),\qquad \lambda v+y-x=e.\] The displayed equality exposes the resolvent-equation error, while the enlargement inclusion exposes the graph-membership error. In particular, \(\varepsilon=0\) and \(e=0\) imply \(v\in T(y)\) and \(x\in y+\lambda T(y)\), hence \(y=J_{\lambda T}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate proximal point is certified by an enlargement graph witness together with an explicit error in the resolvent equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Proximal Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is plausible and fits the terminal container, but its enlargement-based inexact-proximal convention needs a source. The final exact-case derivation is proof text.

children.title: Graph-Membership Conversion
children.top_down_role: Transfers between enlargement-based and proximal-error certificate formats.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}((x,v),\operatorname{gra}T)\) is controlled by the enlargement tolerance through asymmetric primal-dual bounds.

notation.meaning: Positive tradeoff parameter for primal and dual errors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Brøndsted–Rockafellar-type conversion from enlargement membership to nearby exact graph membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every tradeoff parameter \(\rho>0\), enlargement membership \(v\in T^{[\varepsilon]}(x)\) admits an exact graph pair \((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gra}T\) satisfying \[\|x-\bar x\|\leq\rho,
\qquad
\|v-\bar v\|\leq\frac{\varepsilon}{\rho}.\] Thus the enlargement certificate can be converted into exact graph membership at a nearby primal-dual pair. Choosing \(\rho=\sqrt{\varepsilon}\) balances the two reported errors at scale \(\sqrt{\varepsilon}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An enlargement point can be replaced by a nearby exact graph point, with a tunable tradeoff between primal and dual errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Membership Conversion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A Brøndsted–Rockafellar-type theorem is appropriate here, but the precise asymmetric bounds and constants require an authoritative theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Function Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized gap representation for a finite-dimensional variational inequality over a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(x\in C\) and \(\alpha>0\). Define \[g_\alpha(x):=\sup_{y\in C}\left\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|x-y\|^2\right\}.\] Then \(g_\alpha(x)\geq0\), and \[g_\alpha(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\ \text{for every }y\in C\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in F(x)+N_C(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite-dimensional Euclidean space, the regularized gap is nonnegative on the feasible set and vanishes exactly at solutions of the associated variational inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_\alpha(x)\geq0\) and \(g_\alpha(x)=0\iff 0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: Convex-analytic normal cone to the feasible set.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II
source_refs.locator: 10.2.1 The regularized gap function p. 913

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II
source_witnesses.locator: 10.2.1 The regularized gap function p. 913

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of nonnegativity when the regularized gap is evaluated outside its feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\{0\}\subset\mathbb R\), \(F\equiv0\), \(\alpha>0\), and \(x\ne0\), \[g_\alpha(x)=-\frac{\alpha}{2}x^2<0.\] Thus the regularized gap need not be a nonnegative VI certificate outside \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outside the feasible set, even the zero operator can give a negative regularized gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_\alpha(x)=-\alpha x^2/2<0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Boundary for Gap Exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection Representation of the Regularized Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique maximizer and computable projection formula for the Euclidean regularized gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\alpha>0\). For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), the supremum defining \(g_\alpha(x)\) is attained uniquely at \[y_\alpha(x)=P_C\!\left(x-\frac{1}{\alpha}F(x)\right).\] With \(R_\alpha(x):=x-y_\alpha(x)\), \[g_\alpha(x)=\langle F(x),R_\alpha(x)\rangle-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|R_\alpha(x)\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regularized gap has a unique projection-defined maximizer and an explicit natural-residual formula.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_\alpha(x)=P_C(x-F(x)/\alpha)\) uniquely maximizes the defining problem and \(g_\alpha(x)=\langle F(x),R_\alpha(x)\rangle-\alpha\|R_\alpha(x)\|^2/2\).

notation.meaning: Unique maximizer in the regularized-gap definition.
Projection displacement associated with the gap.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Representation of the Regularized Gap

knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Function Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: D-gap merit representation for a finite-dimensional variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and for \(c>0\) define \[g_c(x):=\sup_{y\in C}\left\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-\frac{c}{2}\|x-y\|^2\right\}.\] For \(x\in C\) and \(0<a<b\), define \(G_{a,b}(x):=g_a(x)-g_b(x)\). Then \[G_{a,b}(x)\geq0,\qquad G_{a,b}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in F(x)+N_C(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite-dimensional Euclidean space, the D-gap merit function is nonnegative and vanishes exactly at solutions of the associated variational inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_{a,b}(x):=g_a(x)-g_b(x)\geq0\), and \(G_{a,b}(x)=0\iff 0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: Convex-analytic normal cone to the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), and let \(0<a<b\). Then for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \[G_{a,b}(x):=g_a(x)-g_b(x)\geq0,\qquad G_{a,b}(x)=0\iff x\in C\ \text{and}\ 0\in F(x)+N_C(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unlike a single regularized gap, the D-gap is a globally nonnegative exact merit function on the ambient space.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Scalar Certificate Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative conversion between the natural residual and the regularized gap in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(x\in C\) and \(\alpha>0\). Define \[R_\alpha(x):=x-P_C\bigl(x-F(x)/\alpha\bigr)\] and let \(g_\alpha\) be the regularized gap function. Then \[\frac{\alpha}{2}\|R_\alpha(x)\|^2\leq g_\alpha(x)\leq\|F(x)\|\,\|R_\alpha(x)\|.\] Consequently, for every \(\delta\geq0\), \(g_\alpha(x)\leq\delta\) implies \(\|R_\alpha(x)\|\leq\sqrt{2\delta/\alpha}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite-dimensional Euclidean space, the regularized gap has quadratic and linear bounds in the natural residual; an upper bound on the gap therefore yields an explicit residual certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\|R_\alpha(x)\|^2\leq g_\alpha(x)\leq\|F(x)\|\,\|R_\alpha(x)\|\).

notation.meaning: Natural residual scaled for the regularized-gap parameter.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(0<a<b\). Define \(R_c(x):=x-P_C(x-F(x)/c)\) and \(G_{a,b}(x):=g_a(x)-g_b(x)\). Then \[\frac{b-a}{2}\|R_b(x)\|^2\leq G_{a,b}(x)\leq\frac{b-a}{2}\|R_a(x)\|^2.\] Consequently, \(G_{a,b}(x)\leq\delta\) implies \(\|R_b(x)\|\leq\sqrt{2\delta/(b-a)}\).

children.title: Weak Iterate Convergence
children.top_down_role: Weak-topology convergence regimes for primary iterates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic Consequences of Weak Iterate Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic sequential consequences of weak convergence in a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x_k\rightharpoonup x\) in a real Hilbert space, then the weak limit is unique, \((x_k)\) is norm bounded, and for every \(y\in H\), \[\|x-y\|\leq\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|x_k-y\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly convergent sequence is bounded, has a unique weak limit, and satisfies weak lower semicontinuity of every distance function.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(x_k\rightharpoonup x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_k\|x_k\|<\infty,\qquad \|x-y\|\leq\liminf_k\|x_k-y\|\quad(\forall y\in H).
knowledge_statements.title: Basic Consequences of Weak Iterate Convergence

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \((x_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}\subset H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\rightharpoonup x_\star\iff \langle x_k,z\rangle\to\langle x_\star,z\rangle\) for every \(z\in H\).

notation.meaning: Weak convergence in the Hilbert space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential weak convergence of iterates in a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The iterate sequence \((x_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}\) converges weakly to \(x_\star\), written \(x_k\rightharpoonup x_\star\), when \[\langle x_k,z\rangle\longrightarrow\langle x_\star,z\rangle\qquad\text{for every }z\in H.\] Equivalently, \(f(x_k)\to f(x_\star)\) for every continuous linear functional \(f\in H^*\). Weak iterate convergence does not, in general, imply \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\to0\) in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterates converge weakly when every continuous linear observation of them converges to the corresponding observation of the limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Iterate Convergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and finite- versus infinite-dimensional qualification are correct, but the record has no source or locator.

children.title: Strong Iterate Convergence
children.top_down_role: Norm-topology convergence regimes for primary iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Iterate Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential norm convergence of iterates and its relation to weak convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \((x_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}\subset H\), and let \(x_\star\in H\). The sequence converges strongly to \(x_\star\), written \(x_k\to x_\star\), exactly when \[\|x_k-x_\star\|\longrightarrow0.\] Strong convergence implies weak convergence. In finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, weak and strong sequential convergence coincide; in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, weak convergence generally does not imply strong convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterates converge strongly when their norm distance to the limit tends to zero. Strong convergence implies weak convergence, and the two sequential notions coincide in finite dimensions.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \((x_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}\subset H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to x_\star\) strongly iff \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\to0\); strong convergence implies weak convergence.

notation.meaning: Norm, or strong, convergence in the Hilbert space.

children.title: Topology-Upgrade Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical obstruction to upgrading weak convergence without additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\ell^2\) and let \((e_k)\) be its standard orthonormal basis. Then \(e_k\rightharpoonup0\), whereas \(\|e_k\|=1\) for every \(k\). Thus weak convergence, even together with boundedness, does not imply strong convergence in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard basis of ℓ² converges weakly to zero but stays unit distance from zero.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\ell^2\) and \(e_k\) is its \(k\)-th standard unit vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_k\rightharpoonup0\quad\text{but}\quad e_k\not\to0\text{ strongly}.
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Dimensional Weak-to-Strong Upgrade Failure

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to x\) strongly whenever either \(\|x_k\|\to\|x\|\), or \((x_k)\) is relatively norm-compact and \(x\) is its unique weak cluster point.

notation.meaning: Weak convergence in the Hilbert space
Norm convergence in the Hilbert space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard Hilbert-space mechanisms upgrading weak iterate convergence to norm convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_k)\subset H\) satisfy \(x_k\rightharpoonup x\). Strong convergence \(x_k\to x\) follows under either of the following regimes: \(\|x_k\|\to\|x\|\); or \((x_k)\) is relatively compact in norm and \(x\) is its unique weak cluster point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak convergence upgrades to strong convergence when the norms converge, or when the sequence is norm-precompact and has the weak limit as its unique weak cluster point.
knowledge_statements.title: Topology-Upgrade Regimes

children.title: Shadow-Sequence Convergence
