knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergent Shadow with Divergent Auxiliary Iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between convergence of a resolvent shadow and its generating sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\neq\{0\}\), \(A=N_{\{0\}}\), and \(u\neq0\). Then \(A\) is maximally monotone and \(J_{\gamma A}=P_{\{0\}}=0\). Thus for \(z_k=(-1)^ku\), the auxiliary sequence does not converge, while its shadow \(J_{\gamma A}z_k\) is identically zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant resolvent shadow can converge while its auxiliary iterates oscillate.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a nonzero real Hilbert space, \(A=N_{\{0\}}\), \(u\neq0\), and \(z_k=(-1)^ku\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_k\not\to z_\star\quad\text{while}\quad J_{\gamma A}z_k=0\ \text{for every }k.

notation.meaning: Normal-cone operator of the singleton zero set

knowledge_statements.title: Convergent Shadow with Divergent Auxiliary Iterates

assumptions_latex: \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone, \(\gamma>0\), and \((z_k)\subset H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Shadow-sequence convergence is convergence of \(x_k=J_{\gamma A}z_k\), rather than necessarily convergence of \((z_k)\).

notation.meaning: Identity operator on the Hilbert space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent recovery from auxiliary iterates in monotone splitting methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((z_k)\subset H\), its \(A\)-shadow with parameter \(\gamma\) is the sequence \(x_k=J_{\gamma A}z_k\). Weak shadow convergence to \(x_\star\in H\) means \(x_k\rightharpoonup x_\star\), while strong shadow convergence means \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\to0\). This designation does not require \((z_k)\) to converge in the same topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The shadow sequence is obtained by applying the resolvent to the auxiliary iterates; weak or strong shadow convergence refers to that recovered sequence and not necessarily to the auxiliary sequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Shadow-Sequence Convergence

children.title: Operator-Image Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence of sequences after application of an operator or resolvent-derived map.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong–Weak Closedness of Recovered Graph Pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit identification for resolvent-derived operator values under the two canonical mixed topologies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone and \(a_k\in Ax_k\). If either \(x_k\to x\) strongly and \(a_k\rightharpoonup a\), or \(x_k\rightharpoonup x\) and \(a_k\to a\) strongly, then \(a\in Ax\). Hence either mixed convergence regime identifies the limit of resolvent graph pairs \(x_k=J_{\gamma A}z_k\), \(a_k=\gamma^{-1}(z_k-x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximal monotone graph is closed when one graph component converges strongly and the other weakly.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone, and \(a_k\in Ax_k\).
Either \(x_k\to x\) and \(a_k\rightharpoonup a\), or \(x_k\rightharpoonup x\) and \(a_k\to a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a\in Ax.

notation.meaning: Graph of the maximally monotone operator

knowledge_statements.title: Strong–Weak Closedness of Recovered Graph Pairs

assumptions_latex: \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone, \(\gamma>0\), \((z_k)\subset H\), and \(x_k=J_{\gamma A}z_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence \(a_k=\gamma^{-1}(z_k-x_k)\) satisfies \(a_k\in Ax_k\), and its convergence in a declared topology is operator-image convergence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of graph values induced by a resolvent recovery step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(k\), define \(a_k=\gamma^{-1}(z_k-x_k)\). Then \(a_k\in Ax_k\) and \((x_k,a_k)\in\operatorname{gra}A\). Weak operator-image convergence to \(a_\star\in H\) means \(a_k\rightharpoonup a_\star\), while strong operator-image convergence means \(\|a_k-a_\star\|\to0\). Joint convergence additionally specifies convergence of the graph pairs \((x_k,a_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resolvent step selects an operator value at each recovered point. Operator-image convergence tracks those selected values, with joint convergence also tracking the recovered points.
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Image Convergence

children.title: Recovery-Map Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of convergence information through recovery and transformation maps.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Norm Continuity Does Not Transfer Weak Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary separating norm continuity from weak-topology compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\ell^2\), fix its first basis vector \(e_1\), and define \(R(x)=\|x\|e_1\). Although \(R\) is norm-Lipschitz and \(e_k\rightharpoonup0\), one has \(R(e_k)=e_1\not\rightharpoonup0=R(0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A norm-Lipschitz map can fail to preserve weak convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_k\rightharpoonup0\quad\text{but}\quad R(e_k)\not\rightharpoonup R(0).

notation.meaning: Norm-Lipschitz map not weakly sequentially continuous at zero

knowledge_statements.title: Norm Continuity Does Not Transfer Weak Convergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative strong-error transfer through a locally Lipschitz recovery map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:Z\to X\) satisfy \(\|Rz-Rz_\star\|\leq L\|z-z_\star\|\) near \(z_\star\). If \(\|z_k-z_\star\|=O(r_k)\) with \(r_k\to0\), then \(\|Rz_k-Rz_\star\|=O(r_k)\). In particular, a resolvent \(J_{\gamma A}\) of a maximally monotone Hilbert-space operator transfers strong absolute-error bounds with \(L=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz recovery map preserves absolute strong-error order; a resolvent does so nonexpansively.
assumptions_latex: \(Z,X\) are normed spaces and \(\|Rz-Rz_\star\|\leq L\|z-z_\star\|\) near \(z_\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|Rz_k-Rz_\star\|=O(r_k).
knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Recovery Error Transfer

assumptions_latex: \(R:Z\to X\) is a recovery map between topological spaces.
\(R\) is sequentially continuous from \(\tau_Z\) to a topology \(\tau_X\) at \(z_\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Rz_k\to Rz_\star\) in \(\tau_X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of auxiliary convergence through a topology-compatible recovery map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k=Rz_k\) and \(x_\star=Rz_\star\). If \(z_k\to z_\star\) in \(\tau_Z\) and \(R\) is sequentially \((\tau_Z,\tau_X)\)-continuous at \(z_\star\), then \(x_k\to x_\star\) in \(\tau_X\). In particular, norm continuity transfers strong convergence, while weak-to-strong sequential continuity upgrades weak auxiliary convergence to strong recovery convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence of auxiliary iterates transfers to recovered points whenever the recovery map is sequentially continuous for the chosen source and target topologies.
knowledge_statements.title: Recovery-Map Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequential-continuity transfer principle is precise, uses consistent notation, and fits the recovery-map-transfer leaf. No citation is supplied, so it cannot satisfy the evidence contract.

children.title: Averaging-Pointwise Convergence Dichotomy
children.top_down_role: Averaged-sequence and pointwise guarantee regimes.

children.title: Ergodic Convergence
children.top_down_role: Guarantees for averaged or aggregated iterate sequences.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic mechanism transferring weighted per-iterate certificate bounds to an ergodic iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a real vector space, let \(G:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be convex, and let \(w_k>0\). For \(W_N=\sum_{k=0}^Nw_k\) and \(\bar x_N=W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^Nw_kx_k\), \[G(\bar x_N)\leq\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^Nw_kG(x_k).\] Consequently, \(\sum_{k=0}^Nw_kG(x_k)\leq C_N\) implies \(G(\bar x_N)\leq C_N/W_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity lets a weighted average of per-iterate certificate values control the certificate at the ergodic iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(\bar x_N)\leq W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^Nw_kG(x_k).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Certificate Averaging

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real topological vector space and \((x_k)\subset X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weighted ergodic sequence is \(\bar x_N=W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N}w_kx_k\); point convergence and certificate convergence of this sequence are distinct modes that must be stated separately.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-average convergence, distinct from convergence of individual iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(N\in\mathbb N_0\), define \(\bar x_N=W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N}w_kx_k\). Ergodic point convergence to \(x_\star\in X\) means \(\bar x_N\to x_\star\) in a declared topology. Given a specified functional \(G:X\to[0,+\infty]\), ergodic certificate convergence means \(G(\bar x_N)\to0\); a rate such as \(G(\bar x_N)\le C/W_N\) is an additional quantitative assertion, not part of the definition of point convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ergodic sequence consists of weighted averages. Convergence of those averages and convergence of a certificate evaluated at them are distinct modes and must be identified separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Convergence

children.title: Last-Iterate Convergence
children.top_down_role: Guarantees for the current pointwise iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing-Certificate Failure to Identify a Last Iterate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate decay need not select a single limit when the certificate has multiple zeros.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{-1,1\}\), \(G(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\), and \(x_k=(-1)^k\). Then \(G(x_k)=0\) for every \(k\), but \((x_k)\) does not converge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternation between two solutions gives a zero certificate at every iteration without point convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G(x_k)=0\ \forall k,\qquad x_k\not\to x_\star\ \text{for every }x_\star\in\mathbb R.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Certificate Failure to Identify a Last Iterate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions for weak convergence of the full unaveraged sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and \(C\subset H\) be nonempty. If \(\|x_{k+1}-c\|\leq\|x_k-c\|\) for every \(c\in C\) and every \(k\), and every weak sequential cluster point of \((x_k)\) belongs to \(C\), then \(x_k\rightharpoonup x_\star\) for some \(x_\star\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fejér monotonicity and identification of every weak cluster point imply weak convergence of the complete last-iterate sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(C\subset H\) is nonempty.
Every weak sequential cluster point of \((x_k)\) lies in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\rightharpoonup x_\star\quad\text{for some }x_\star\in C.
knowledge_statements.title: Fejér–Opial Criterion for Last-Iterate Convergence

assumptions_latex: \((x_k)\subset X\) is the unaveraged sequence produced by an iterative method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Last-iterate convergence requires \(x_k\to x_\star\), or a stated certificate \(G(x_k)\to0\), without averaging over earlier iterates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise-in-iteration convergence of the current iterate or its certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Last-iterate convergence to \(x_\star\) means that the current iterate itself satisfies \(x_k\to x_\star\) in the declared topology. A last-iterate certificate rate has the form \(G(x_k)\le r_k\), where \(G\ge0\) vanishes on the target solution set and \(r_k\to0\). No Cesàro or weighted averaging of \(x_0,\ldots,x_k\) is permitted in this designation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Last-iterate convergence requires the current iterate, or its own certificate, to converge without averaging previous iterates.
knowledge_statements.title: Last-Iterate Convergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes an unaveraged current-iterate assertion from ergodic averaging and fits the exact leaf. A source with a specific locator is absent.

children.title: Averaging-to-Pointwise Separation
children.top_down_role: Boundaries preventing ergodic guarantees from transferring to last iterates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The valid implication opposite to the immutable averaging-to-pointwise counterexample.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space, let \(x_k\to x\), and let \(w_k>0\) with \(W_N=\sum_{k=0}^Nw_k\to+\infty\). Then \[\bar x_N=\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^Nw_kx_k\to x.\] Thus last-iterate convergence implies convergence of these weighted averages to the same limit, whereas the converse can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive weighted averaging with diverging cumulative weight preserves an existing last-iterate limit; only the converse implication fails in general.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space and \(x_k\to x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^Nw_kx_k\to x.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Regularity of Weighted Averaging

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x_N\to0\), while \((x_k)\) does not converge.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary separation between convergence of averages and convergence of current iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the real sequence \(x_k=(-1)^k\), the Cesàro averages satisfy \(\bar x_N=0\) for odd \(N\) and \(\bar x_N=(N+1)^{-1}\) for even \(N\). Thus \(\bar x_N\to0\), whereas \((x_k)\) does not converge. Consequently, ergodic convergence does not in general imply last-iterate convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The alternating real sequence has Cesàro averages converging to zero while its individual iterates do not converge, so ergodic convergence does not imply last-iterate convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Averaging-to-Pointwise Separation

children.title: Quantitative Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Rate families classified by operator regularity and certificate type.

children.title: General-Monotone Sublinear Regimes
children.top_down_role: Residual and ergodic rate families without strong regularity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ergodic Enlargement Certificate for the Proximal-Point Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-one ergodic certificate in the general maximal-monotone regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_i=J_{\lambda A}x_{i-1}\), \(v_i=(x_{i-1}-x_i)/\lambda\in A(x_i)\), and for \(N\ge1\) define \(\bar x_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N x_i\), \(\bar v_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N v_i\), and \(\bar\varepsilon_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\langle x_i-\bar x_N,v_i-\bar v_N\rangle\). Then \(\bar\varepsilon_N\ge0\), \(\bar v_N\in A^{[\bar\varepsilon_N]}(\bar x_N)\), and, for \(x_\star\in\operatorname{zer}A\) and \(d_0=\|x_0-x_\star\|\), \(\|\bar v_N\|\le2d_0/(\lambda N)\) and \(\bar\varepsilon_N\le5d_0^2/(2\lambda N)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averages of exact proximal-point graph pairs give an enlargement certificate whose vector residual and enlargement tolerance decay as one over the iteration count.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar v_N\in A^{[\bar\varepsilon_N]}(\bar x_N)\), \(\|\bar v_N\|=O(N^{-1})\), and \(\bar\varepsilon_N=O(N^{-1})\).
knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Enlargement Certificate for the Proximal-Point Iteration

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Last-Iterate Asymptotic Regularity for Firmly Nonexpansive Picard Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise residual rate without strong regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=Tx_k\), where \(T:H\to H\) is firmly nonexpansive and \(x_\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\). With \(r_k=\|x_k-Tx_k\|\), the sequence \((r_k)\) is nonincreasing, \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}r_k^2\le\|x_0-x_\star\|^2\), \(r_k\le\|x_0-x_\star\|/\sqrt{k+1}\), and \(r_k=o(k^{-1/2})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Firm nonexpansiveness gives square-summable, nonincreasing residuals, a last-iterate inverse-square-root bound, and a little-o refinement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}r_k^2\le\|x_0-x_\star\|^2\), \(r_k\le\|x_0-x_\star\|/\sqrt{k+1}\), and \(\sqrt{k}r_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Last-Iterate Asymptotic Regularity for Firmly Nonexpansive Picard Iteration

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Uniform Linear Residual Rate for Firmly Nonexpansive Iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral obstruction to a class-wide geometric rate in the general firmly nonexpansive regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\ell^2\) and \(T(x_1,x_2,\ldots)=(t_1x_1,t_2x_2,\ldots)\), where \(0<t_j<1\) and \(t_j\uparrow1\). Then \(T\) is firmly nonexpansive and \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\{0\}\). For \(x_0=e_j\), \[\|x_k-Tx_k\|=(1-t_j)t_j^k.\] Hence no constants \(C<\infty\) and \(q<1\) satisfy \(\|x_k-Tx_k\|\leq Cq^k\|x_0-Tx_0\|\) uniformly over this class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal firmly nonexpansive maps with eigenvalues approaching one rule out a uniform geometric residual rate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nexists\,C<\infty,\ q<1\text{ giving the stated class-wide geometric bound}.

notation.meaning: The j-th standard basis vector of \(\ell^2\)

knowledge_statements.title: No Uniform Linear Residual Rate for Firmly Nonexpansive Iterations

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{0\le k\le N}\|x_k-Tx_k\|\le \|x_0-x_\star\|/\sqrt{N+1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-iterate residual bound for firmly nonexpansive fixed-point iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(N\in\mathbb N_0\), the fixed-point residuals satisfy \(\min_{0\le k\le N}\|x_k-Tx_k\|\le \|x_0-x_\star\|/\sqrt{N+1}\). Hence a best-iterate residual not exceeding \(\varepsilon>0\) is guaranteed whenever \(N+1\ge \|x_0-x_\star\|^2/\varepsilon^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Firmly nonexpansive fixed-point iteration has a best-iterate residual bounded by the initial distance divided by the square root of the horizon; this gives an inverse-square residual complexity guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: General-Monotone Sublinear Regimes

children.title: Linear Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric regimes induced by contraction, strong monotonicity, or error bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Metric-Subregularity-Induced Linear Rate for Averaged Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local geometric distance convergence from averagedness and a residual error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged, \(0<\alpha<1\), and let \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\). Suppose on a Picard-invariant neighborhood \(U\) that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa\|x-Tx\|\), with \(\kappa^2>(1-\alpha)/\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{dist}(Tx,S)\le q\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\), where \(q=\sqrt{1-(1-\alpha)/(\alpha\kappa^2)}<1\), and Picard iterates starting in \(U\) satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\le q^k\operatorname{dist}(x_0,S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an averaged map, a local residual error bound converts Fejér decrease into a local geometric distance rate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\le q^k\operatorname{dist}(x_0,S)\), where \(q=\sqrt{1-(1-\alpha)/(\alpha\kappa^2)}<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Subregularity-Induced Linear Rate for Averaged Maps

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Proximal-Point Regime under Strong Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global geometric convergence of a resolvent iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally \(m\)-strongly monotone with \(m>0\), then \(J_{\lambda A}\) is Lipschitz with constant \((1+\lambda m)^{-1}\). If \(x_\star\in\operatorname{zer}A\), the iteration \(x_{k+1}=J_{\lambda A}x_k\) satisfies \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\le(1+\lambda m)^{-k}\|x_0-x_\star\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong monotonicity makes the resolvent contractive and yields a global geometric proximal-point rate.
assumptions_latex: \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally \(m\)-strongly monotone for some \(m>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\le(1+\lambda m)^{-k}\|x_0-x_\star\|\).
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Proximal-Point Regime under Strong Monotonicity

assumptions_latex: \(T:H\to H\) satisfies \(\|Tx-Ty\|\le q\|x-y\|\) for every \(x,y\in H\), where \(q\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\le q^k d_0\); for \(q\in(0,1)\) this gives logarithmic distance complexity, while \(q=0\) gives convergence after one iteration.

notation.meaning: Initial distance to the fixed point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global geometric convergence induced by a contractive iteration map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(k\in\mathbb N_0\), \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\le q^k d_0\). If \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(0<\varepsilon<d_0\), then \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\le\varepsilon\) is guaranteed for every \(k\ge\left\lceil\log(d_0/\varepsilon)/(-\log q)\right\rceil\). If \(q=0\), then \(x_k=x_\star\) for every \(k\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contraction gives geometric error decay. For a positive contraction factor the distance complexity is logarithmic, while a zero contraction factor reaches the fixed point after one iteration.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Convergence Regimes

children.title: Optimized Anchored Residual Regimes
children.top_down_role: Residual improvements obtained through anchoring and optimized coefficients.

children.title: Anchored Residual Regimes
children.top_down_role: Residual guarantees attributable to explicit anchoring.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonasymptotic residual bound for the harmonic anchor schedule on a bounded invariant set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) have diameter at most \(D\), let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive, set \(x_0=u\in C\), and iterate \[x_{k+1}=\frac{1}{k+2}u+\frac{k+1}{k+2}Tx_k.\] Then \[\|x_k-Tx_k\|\leq\frac{2D}{k+1}\qquad(k\geq0).\] Thus \(k+1\geq2D/\varepsilon\) suffices for an \(\varepsilon\)-residual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The harmonic Halpern iteration on a bounded invariant convex set has an order-one last-iterate residual bound.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty convex subset of a real Hilbert space with \(\operatorname{diam}C\leq D<\infty\).

notation.meaning: Upper bound on the invariant domain's diameter

knowledge_statements.title: Order-One Halpern Residual Bound

assumptions_latex: \(T:C\to C\) is nonexpansive on a closed convex subset \(C\) of a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An anchored residual regime studies \(r_k=\|x_k-Tx_k\|\) along \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_{k+1}u+(1-\alpha_{k+1})Tx_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Halpern-type anchored iteration classified by its fixed-point residual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The anchored iteration is \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_{k+1}u+(1-\alpha_{k+1})Tx_k\). Its residual regime is the asymptotic or nonasymptotic behavior of \(r_k=\|x_k-Tx_k\|\). An order-one anchored residual certificate has the form \(r_k\le C/(k+1)\), where \(C\) is independent of \(k\) but may depend on the initial point, anchor, operator, and feasible-set diameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An anchored residual regime records fixed-point residual decay for a Halpern-type iteration combining a fixed anchor with the operator image.
knowledge_statements.title: Anchored Residual Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the anchored-residual leaf and does not assert that the displayed order-one certificate follows from the generic assumptions. However, the Halpern terminology and the stated benchmark require a specific authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Iterate Convergence Implies Residual Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic fixed-point consequence not specific enough for primary placement under anchored residual regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(T:C\to C\) is nonexpansive, \(p\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), and \(x_k\to p\) strongly, then \(\|x_k-Tx_k\|\le2\|x_k-p\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convergence to a fixed point forces the fixed-point residual to vanish.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Iterate Convergence Implies Residual Convergence

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns the Halpern-type anchored iteration and quantitative decay of its fixed-point residual. The exact order-one theorem remains missing, so expansion is required. Coefficient admissibility and accelerated coefficient design are excluded to sibling leaves; generic fixed-point residual implications belong at the residual-certificate node.

children.title: Accelerated Residual Regimes
children.top_down_role: Residual guarantees attributable to optimized coefficient choices.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(T:H\to H\), and \((x_k)\subset H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relative to the benchmark \(r_k=O(k^{-1})\), accelerated residual decay means \(r_k=o(k^{-1})\); a polynomial accelerated certificate has the form \(r_k\le C(k+1)^{-p}\) with \(C>0\) and \(p>1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate classification relative to the order-one anchored residual benchmark.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Relative to the benchmark \(r_k=O(k^{-1})\), an accelerated residual regime is characterized by \(r_k=o(k^{-1})\), equivalently \(kr_k\to0\). A polynomial accelerated certificate specifies constants \(C>0\) and \(p>1\) such that \(r_k\le C/(k+1)^p\) for all indices in the stated range. This is a rate classification; any claim that an algorithm attains it requires separate algorithmic and structural hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to an order-one-over-iteration benchmark, accelerated residual decay is little-o of that benchmark; polynomial acceleration uses an exponent greater than one and requires separate algorithm-specific justification.
knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Residual Regimes

children.title: Coefficient-Optimization Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on residual improvement from coefficient design.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Summable Anchor Weights Need Not Select the Anchor Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing the need for infinite cumulative anchor influence in universal anchor selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\mathbb R\), \(T=I\), \(u=1\), \(x_0=0\), and choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1)\) with \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\alpha_k<\infty\). Then \(x_k=1-\prod_{j=1}^{k}(1-\alpha_j)\), and the infinite product is positive. Hence \(x_k\) converges to a point different from \(1=P_{\operatorname{Fix}T}u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If total anchor influence is finite, even the identity map need not select the projection of the anchor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\not\to P_{\operatorname{Fix}T}u\).
knowledge_statements.title: Summable Anchor Weights Need Not Select the Anchor Projection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonvanishing Anchor Weights Can Prevent Fixed-Point Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing the need for vanishing anchor influence in universal Halpern convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=C=\mathbb R\), \(T(x)=0\), \(u=1\), and \(\alpha_k\equiv a\in(0,1]\). Then \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\{0\}\), while the anchored iteration satisfies \(x_{k+1}=a\) for every \(k\). It therefore does not converge to \(P_{\operatorname{Fix}T}u=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A persistent positive anchor weight can keep the anchored iteration away from the fixed-point set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k=a\) for every \(k\ge1\), so \(x_k\not\to P_{\operatorname{Fix}T}u\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonvanishing Anchor Weights Can Prevent Fixed-Point Convergence

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(T:C\to C\) is nonexpansive with \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to P_{\operatorname{Fix}T}u\) strongly; the displayed coefficient requirements are sufficient and are not asserted to be necessary.

notation.meaning: Metric projection onto the fixed-point set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical sufficient coefficient constraints for strong convergence of Halpern iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The coefficient conditions \(\alpha_k\in(0,1)\), \(\alpha_k\to0\), \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\alpha_k=+\infty\), and \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|\alpha_{k+1}-\alpha_k|<+\infty\) are sufficient for the Halpern iterates to converge strongly to \(P_{\operatorname{Fix}T}u\). These conditions are not asserted to be necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonexpansive map with a fixed point, vanishing nonsummable anchor weights with summable successive variation are sufficient for strong convergence of the Halpern iterates to the projection of the anchor onto the fixed-point set; necessity is not claimed.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Optimization Boundaries

children.title: Fast Local Solver Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Local fast-convergence interfaces delegated to generalized-equation solvers.

children.title: Local Newton Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Connections to local Newton-type generalized-equation solvers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximal Monotonicity Does Not Ensure Newton Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary obstruction to a nonsingular Newton model for the Yosida residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\neq\{0\}\) and \(A(x)=\{0\}\) for every \(x\in H\). Then \(A\) is maximally monotone, \(J_{\lambda A}=I\), and \(A_\lambda=\lambda^{-1}(I-J_{\lambda A})\equiv0\). Thus \(\operatorname{zer}A=H\), and every classical derivative of \(A_\lambda\), as well as every standard generalized derivative containing only its linearization, is noninvertible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero maximal-monotone operator has an identically zero Yosida residual, so maximal monotonicity alone supplies neither an isolated solution nor an invertible Newton model.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a nonzero real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_\lambda\equiv0\), \(\operatorname{zer}A=H\), and the zero linearization is noninvertible.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximal Monotonicity Does Not Ensure Newton Regularity

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone.
\(\bar x\in\operatorname{zer}A\), and the Yosida residual \(F_\lambda=\lambda^{-1}(I-J_{\lambda A})\) is semismooth near \(\bar x\).
Every matrix in the generalized Jacobian \(\partial F_\lambda(\bar x)\) is nonsingular, with locally uniformly bounded inverses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=x^k-V_k^{-1}F_\lambda(x^k)\) is locally well-defined and converges superlinearly to \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: Generalized Jacobian element at the current iterate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismooth Newton interface for a resolvent-based residual in a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\lambda>0\). A local Newton interface for \(0\in A(x)\) is available at \(\bar x\) when \(F_\lambda(\bar x)=0\), \(F_\lambda\) is semismooth near \(\bar x\), and every \(V\in\partial F_\lambda(\bar x)\) is invertible with locally uniformly bounded inverse. For an initial point sufficiently near \(\bar x\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F_\lambda(x^k)\), solve \(V_kd^k=-F_\lambda(x^k)\), and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+d^k\). Under these conditions the steps are locally well-defined and \(\|x^{k+1}-\bar x\|/\|x^k-\bar x\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A semismooth resolvent residual with uniformly invertible generalized Jacobians supplies Newton steps that converge locally superlinearly to a solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Newton Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asserted semismooth Newton theorem depends on the precise generalized derivative and semismoothness notion. The Hilbert-space formulation and neighborhood-wide invertibility conditions require a targeted source before the hypotheses and superlinear conclusion can be trusted.

children.title: Local Regularization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Connections to locally regularized generalized-equation solvers.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Regularization Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly monotone regularization of the Yosida equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\lambda>0\), an anchor \(\bar x\in H\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and parameters \(\mu_k>0\). At iteration \(k\), compute the unique \(x^{k+1}\in H\) satisfying \[0=A_\lambda(x^{k+1})+\mu_k(x^{k+1}-\bar x).\] Stop and return \(x^{k+1}\) when \(\lVert A_\lambda(x^{k+1})\rVert\leq\varepsilon\). In a continuation implementation, choose \(\mu_k\downarrow0\) and solve each regularized equation to its prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a uniquely determined, strongly monotone regularization of the Yosida equation and, for continuation, reduce the positive regularization parameter toward zero.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(k\), the regularized inclusion has a unique solution \(x^{k+1}\), and \(A_\lambda(x^{k+1})=-\mu_k(x^{k+1}-\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of vanishing-regularization selection when the original zero set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(H=\mathbb R\), let \(A(x)=\{1\}\). Then \(A\) is maximally monotone, \(A_\lambda\equiv1\), and the unique solution of \(0=A_\lambda(x_\mu)+\mu(x_\mu-a)\) is \(x_\mu=a-\mu^{-1}\). Consequently \(|x_\mu|\to\infty\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\), while \(\operatorname{zer}A=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the operator has no zero, exact regularized solutions can diverge as regularization vanishes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\mu=a-\mu^{-1}\) and \(|x_\mu|\to\infty\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: Solution of the regularized Yosida equation

knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Zero-Set Regularization Can Diverge

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tikhonov Regularization Selects the Nearest Zero
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong limit of exact vanishing-regularization solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z=\operatorname{zer}A\neq\varnothing\), fix \(a\in H\), and for each \(\mu>0\) let \(x_\mu\) be the unique solution of \(0=A_\lambda x_\mu+\mu(x_\mu-a)\). Then \(x_\mu\to P_Za\) strongly as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact Tikhonov regularizations of the Yosida equation converge to the zero nearest the anchor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\mu\to P_{\operatorname{zer}A}a\) in norm as \(\mu\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: Metric projection of the anchor onto the zero set

children.title: Fast-Local-Regime Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of local fast-convergence regimes to specialized solver chapters.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of residual-to-iterate rate transfer without a local residual error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F(0)=0\) and \(F(x)=e^{-1/x^2}\) for \(x\neq0\), and take \(x^k=1/k\). Then \[\frac{|F(x^{k+1})|}{|F(x^k)|}=e^{-(2k+1)}\to0,\qquad \frac{|x^{k+1}|}{|x^k|}=\frac{k}{k+1}\to1.\] Thus superlinear residual decay need not imply Q-linear iterate convergence without a local error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinitely flat residual decays superlinearly along 1/k although the iterates converge only sublinearly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{|F(x^{k+1})|}{|F(x^k)|}\to0\quad\text{but}\quad\frac{|x^{k+1}|}{|x^k|}\to1.

notation.meaning: Residual infinitely flat at its zero

knowledge_statements.title: Flat-Residual Failure of Fast-Rate Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Q-linear counterpart of the seed's superlinear transfer result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F(\bar x)=0\) and, near \(\bar x\), \(\|x-\bar x\|\leq\kappa\|F(x)\|\) and \(\|F(x)\|\leq L\|x-\bar x\|\). If an eventually local sequence satisfies \(\|F(x^{k+1})\|\leq q\|F(x^k)\|\), then \[\|x^{k+1}-\bar x\|\leq\kappa Lq\,\|x^k-\bar x\|.\] Hence \(\kappa Lq<1\) certifies Q-linear iterate convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-sided local residual control converts a residual contraction into an iterate contraction with certified factor κLq.
assumptions_latex: \(F(\bar x)=0\) and locally \(\|x-\bar x\|\leq\kappa\|F(x)\|\) and \(\|F(x)\|\leq L\|x-\bar x\|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x^{k+1}-\bar x\|\leq\kappa Lq\|x^k-\bar x\|;\qquad \kappa Lq<1\Rightarrow Q\text{-linear convergence}.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Residual-to-Iterate Rate Transfer
Fast-Local-Regime Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer from superlinear residual decay to superlinear iterate convergence under two-sided local residual control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:H\to H\) satisfy \(F(\bar x)=0\). Suppose that, on a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), \[\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\leq\kappa\lVert F(x)\rVert\quad\text{and}\quad\lVert F(x)\rVert\leq L\lVert x-\bar x\rVert.\] If \(x^k\in U\), \(x^k\neq\bar x\) eventually, and \[\frac{\lVert F(x^{k+1})\rVert}{\lVert F(x^k)\rVert}\longrightarrow0,\] then \[\frac{\lVert x^{k+1}-\bar x\rVert}{\lVert x^k-\bar x\rVert}\longrightarrow0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local error bound together with a local Lipschitz residual bound transfers superlinear residual decay to superlinear convergence of the iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(F:H\to H\), and \(F(\bar x)=0\).

There are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and constants \(\kappa,L>0\) such that \(\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\leq\kappa\lVert F(x)\rVert\) and \(\lVert F(x)\rVert\leq L\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\) for every \(x\in U\).
\(x^k\in U\), \(x^k\neq\bar x\) eventually, and \(\lVert F(x^{k+1})\rVert/\lVert F(x^k)\rVert\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x^{k+1}-\bar x\rVert/\lVert x^k-\bar x\rVert\to0\).

notation.meaning: Neighborhood on which both residual bounds hold

children.title: Nonmaximal Graph Failures
children.top_down_role: Graph-level pathologies caused by failure of maximal monotonicity.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonmaximal Graph Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of full-domain resolvent behavior without maximality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathbb R\rightrightarrows\mathbb R\) be defined by \(A(0)=\{0\}\) and \(A(x)=\varnothing\) for \(x\neq0\). Then \(A\) is monotone but not maximally monotone. For every \(\lambda>0\), its resolvent satisfies \[J_{\lambda A}(0)=0,\qquad J_{\lambda A}(y)=\varnothing\quad(y\neq0).\] Thus a monotone nonmaximal operator need not have an everywhere-defined resolvent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The single-point zero graph is monotone but nonmaximal, and its resolvent is defined only at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) is monotone but not maximally monotone, and \(\operatorname{dom}J_{\lambda A}=\{0\}\).

children.title: Resolvent Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures of global resolvent availability or regular behavior.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_A(0)=\mathbb R\) and \(J_A(y)=\varnothing\) for \(y\neq0\), so the resolvent is neither single-valued nor full-domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete resolvent failure when monotonicity is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(A:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) by \(A(x)=-x\). Then \(I+A\) is the zero mapping. Hence the inverse relation satisfies \(J_A(0)=\mathbb R\), while \(J_A(y)=\varnothing\) for every \(y\neq0\). Thus the nominal resolvent is multivalued at the origin and undefined elsewhere. This example shows that, without monotonicity and maximality hypotheses, the expression \((I+\lambda A)^{-1}\) need not define a single-valued mapping on the ambient Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the antimonotone map minus the identity, the unit-step resolvent is multivalued at zero and undefined elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is internally precise and fits the resolvent-failure leaf, but it has no citation. A targeted source is required before retaining the claim as candidate-review knowledge.

children.title: Partial-Domain Resolvent Behavior
children.top_down_role: Resolvent behavior restricted to a proper subset of the ambient space.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Domain Resolvent Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent properties on the natural range when maximality is not assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be monotone and let \(\lambda>0\). On \(D_\lambda=\operatorname{ran}(I+\lambda A)\), the resolvent \(J_{\lambda A}\) is single-valued and satisfies \[\lVert J_{\lambda A}p-J_{\lambda A}q\rVert^2\leq\big\langle J_{\lambda A}p-J_{\lambda A}q,p-q\big\rangle\qquad(p,q\in D_\lambda).\] Its domain is all of \(H\) exactly when \(D_\lambda=H\). Without maximality, \(D_\lambda\) may be a proper subset of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone operator's resolvent is single-valued and firmly nonexpansive on its natural domain, which may be smaller than the whole space.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is monotone, and \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_{\lambda A}\) is single-valued and firmly nonexpansive on \(D_\lambda=\operatorname{ran}(I+\lambda A)\), and \(D_\lambda\) may be a proper subset of \(H\).

children.title: Inconsistency Surrogate-Target Regimes
children.top_down_role: Surrogate targets when the original zero set is empty.

children.title: Inconsistent Inclusion Regimes
children.top_down_role: Monotone inclusion regimes with an empty zero set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Inconsistency with Linear Proximal Drift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly inconsistent maximal-monotone inclusion whose proximal displacement remains nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be the constant operator \(A(x)=1\). It is maximally monotone, \(\operatorname{zer}A=\varnothing\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\operatorname{ran}A)=1\). For every \(\lambda>0\), \(J_{\lambda A}(y)=y-\lambda\), so the proximal iteration satisfies \(x^k=x^0-k\lambda\to-\infty\) and \(|x^{k+1}-x^k|=\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant maximal-monotone operator gives a strongly inconsistent inclusion whose proximal iterates drift linearly with persistent displacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{zer}A=\varnothing\), \(x^k=x^0-k\lambda\to-\infty\), and \(|x^{k+1}-x^k|=\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Inconsistency with Linear Proximal Drift

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range-distance classification of an inclusion with an empty zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an operator \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) with \(\operatorname{zer}A=\varnothing\), the inconsistency is strong when \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\operatorname{ran}A)>0\), and weak when \(0\in\overline{\operatorname{ran}A}\setminus\operatorname{ran}A\). These alternatives exhaust the empty-zero-set case according to whether the unattained residual infimum is positive or zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inconsistent inclusion is strong when operator values stay positively away from zero and weak when zero is only an unattained range limit.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\operatorname{ran}A)>0\), or \(0\in\overline{\operatorname{ran}A}\setminus\operatorname{ran}A\).

notation.meaning: Set of solutions to the inclusion \(0\in A(x)\)

knowledge_statements.title: Strong and Weak Inconsistency Regimes

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{zer}A=\varnothing\), \(x^k\to-\infty\), and \(|x^{k+1}-x^k|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inconsistent maximal-monotone inclusion with vanishing displacement but no solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The continuous increasing map \(A(x)=e^x\) is maximally monotone on \(\mathbb R\), but \(0\in A(x)\) has no solution. Its proximal iteration obeys \(x^k=x^{k+1}+\lambda e^{x^{k+1}}\), so \(x^{k+1}<x^k\). A finite limit would satisfy \(e^x=0\), which is impossible; hence \(x^k\to-\infty\). Nevertheless, \(|x^{k+1}-x^k|=\lambda e^{x^{k+1}}\to0\). Thus vanishing fixed-point displacement does not certify solvability when the inclusion is inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the exponential monotone operator, the inclusion has no zero; proximal iterates diverge to minus infinity even though successive displacements vanish.
knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Inclusion Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exponential example is plausible and appropriately classified as a failure boundary, but no source supports maximal monotonicity, the divergent proximal orbit, and vanishing displacement as one cited claim.

children.title: Normal-Problem Replacements
children.top_down_role: Normal-problem targets used when the original inclusion is inconsistent.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normal replacement is \(x-Tx=v\), equivalently \(x\in\operatorname{Fix}(v+T)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal-displacement normal problem for an inconsistent firmly nonexpansive fixed-point equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\varnothing\), define the minimal displacement vector by \(v=P_{\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}}0\). The associated normal problem replaces \(x=Tx\) by \[x-Tx=v.\] Its solution set has the equivalent representation \[\{x\in H:x-Tx=v\}=\operatorname{Fix}(v+T).\] This set is nonempty precisely when the minimal displacement vector is attained by \(I-T\), namely when \(v\in\operatorname{ran}(I-T)\). If attainment fails, the normal replacement itself has no exact solution and must be interpreted through approximate displacement sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inconsistent fixed-point equation is replaced by matching the minimal displacement vector; exact normal solutions exist only when that displacement is attained.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Problem Replacements

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and attainment distinction are standard but nontrivial. A source specifically addressing minimal displacement vectors and normal solutions for firmly nonexpansive mappings is required.

children.title: Surrogate-Target Selection
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria governing the replacement target associated with inconsistency.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Use \(\operatorname{Fix}(v+T)\) when \(v\) is attained; otherwise target sequences satisfying \((I-T)x^k\to v\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection rule distinguishing attained and unattained minimal displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select the surrogate target according to attainment of the minimal displacement. If \(v\in\operatorname{ran}(I-T)\), use the exact normal-solution set \(\operatorname{Fix}(v+T)\) and certify a candidate \(x\) by \(r_v(x)=0\). If \(v\notin\operatorname{ran}(I-T)\), no exact normal solution exists; use approximate targets \((x^k)\) satisfying \(\|r_v(x^k)\|\to0\), together with any additional boundedness or application-specific selection criterion needed to identify meaningful primal variables. The original fixed-point residual must not be interpreted as an exact-solution certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose exact normal solutions when minimal displacement is attained; otherwise use sequences whose displacement approaches the unattained minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate-Target Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The attained-versus-unattained selection principle fits the leaf, but its normal-problem interpretation and approximate-target prescription require targeted support.

children.title: Algorithmic Error-Instability Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Instability caused by incompatible controls or accumulated errors.

children.title: Parameter Instability
children.top_down_role: Instability caused by incompatible or poorly controlled parameter regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of relaxed proximal iteration at and beyond the upper relaxation boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=N_{\{0\}}\) on \(\mathbb R\), so \(J_{\lambda A}=0\) for every \(\lambda>0\). The relaxed proximal iteration \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha(J_{\lambda A}x^k-x^k)\) satisfies \(x^{k+1}=(1-\alpha)x^k\). For \(x^0\neq0\), \(\alpha=2\) produces a nonconvergent two-cycle and \(\alpha>2\) produces unbounded iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a resolvent equal to zero, relaxation two causes a two-cycle and relaxation above two causes divergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha=2\) yields \(x^{k+1}=-x^k\), while \(\alpha>2\) yields \(|x^k|=|1-\alpha|^k|x^0|\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: Normal-cone operator of the singleton zero set

knowledge_statements.title: Overrelaxation Instability Boundary

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\to x^0\prod_{j=0}^{\infty}(1+\lambda_j)^{-1}\neq0\), although \(\operatorname{zer}A=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by a summable proximal parameter sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A=I\), the variable-parameter proximal iteration is \[x^{k+1}=\frac{x^k}{1+\lambda_k},\qquad x^k=x^0\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(1+\lambda_j)^{-1}.\] Because \(\sum_j\lambda_j<\infty\), the infinite product \(\prod_j(1+\lambda_j)\) converges to a finite positive number. Hence every nonzero initial point produces a nonzero limiting iterate, despite the unique zero \(\operatorname{zer}A=\{0\}\). Thus allowing the cumulative proximal parameter to remain finite can destroy convergence to a solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the identity operator, summable proximal step sizes yield a nonzero limit, so the iteration misses the unique zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter Instability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The variable-step counterexample is mathematically coherent and correctly classified, but no inspectable source is supplied for the convergence failure associated with a finite cumulative proximal parameter.

children.title: Inexactness Instability
children.top_down_role: Instability caused by accumulated computational approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexactness Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing but nonsummable deterministic errors can prevent iterate convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\mathbb R\), \(A=0\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(e_k=(k+1)^{-1}\). For the inexact proximal iteration \[x^{k+1}=J_{\lambda A}x^k+e_k,\] one has \[x^k=x^0+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{1}{j+1}\longrightarrow+\infty,\] although \(e_k\to0\). Thus pointwise decay of deterministic errors does not by itself ensure convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing harmonic errors accumulate under the identity resolvent and make the iterates diverge; pointwise error decay alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k=x^0+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}e_j\to+\infty\), despite \(e_k\to0\).

children.title: Persistent-Noise Instability
children.top_down_role: Instability caused by nonvanishing stochastic or deterministic disturbances.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonvanishing independent noise in a contractive scalar iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\in(0,1)\), let \((\xi_k)\) be independent Rademacher random variables, and set \(x^{k+1}=qx^k+\xi_{k+1}\) from a deterministic \(x^0\). Then \((x^k)\) does not converge almost surely, and \(\mathbb E[(x^k)^2]\to(1-q^2)^{-1}\). Thus contraction does not remove persistent stochastic variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent nonvanishing noise prevents almost-sure convergence of a scalar contraction and leaves a positive limiting variance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\) does not converge almost surely and \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\mathbb E[(x^k)^2]=(1-q^2)^{-1}>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Stochastic-Variance Instability

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\to e(1+\lambda)/\lambda\neq0\), so persistent noise creates a nonzero asymptotic bias.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant deterministic noise produces a bias even for a strongly monotone linear operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Since \(J_{\lambda A}=(1+\lambda)^{-1}I\), the perturbed iteration is \(x^{k+1}=qx^k+e\), where \(q=(1+\lambda)^{-1}\in(0,1)\). It converges from every initial point to \[x_e=\frac{e}{1-q}=\frac{1+\lambda}{\lambda}e.\] The exact inclusion has the unique solution \(0\), but \(x_e\neq0\) whenever \(e\neq0\). Thus contraction suppresses transients but cannot remove persistent additive noise; it yields convergence to a noise-dependent neighborhood or biased point rather than to the exact zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant additive error in a contractive proximal iteration produces a stable but nonzero bias instead of convergence to the exact solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Noise Instability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The persistent-bias example is internally consistent and fits the failure-boundary container, but it lacks an inspectable citation supporting the perturbation model and asymptotic-bias claim.

children.title: Error-Accumulation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Comparative regimes for transient, summable, and persistent error effects.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\|e_k\|<\infty\) controls total perturbation, whereas square summability alone does not prevent unbounded drift.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit identity-operator example establishes the accumulation boundary
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes absolute summability from weaker error controls for perturbed nonexpansive iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the perturbed iteration \(x_{k+1}=Tx_k+e_k\), absolute summability \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|e_k\|<\infty\) implies that the cumulative displacement caused directly by the errors is finite. This boundary cannot generally be weakened to \(\sum_k\|e_k\|^2<\infty\): take \(H=\mathbb R\), \(T=I\), and \(e_k=(k+1)^{-1}\). Then \(T\) is nonexpansive with every point fixed and \(\sum_k|e_k|^2<\infty\), but \(x_k=x_0+\sum_{j<k}(j+1)^{-1}\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolutely summable errors have finite cumulative effect; square-summable errors may still accumulate and drive even an identity fixed-point iteration to infinity.
knowledge_statements.title: Error-Accumulation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample and failure-boundary classification are mathematically correct, but the record has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Residual Decay without Iterate Convergence
children.top_down_role: Separation between approximate stationarity and orbit convergence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient local condition converting residual decay into convergence to a specified isolated zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\), let \(x_\star\in\operatorname{zer}A\), and suppose that for a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x_\star\) and \(\kappa>0\), \[\|x-x_\star\|\leq\kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(0,Ax)\qquad(x\in U).\] If \(x_k\in U\) eventually and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,Ax_k)\to0\), then \(x_k\to x_\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local pointwise residual error bound converts residual decay into convergence to the specified zero, provided the iterates eventually remain in its neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,Ax_k)\to0\Longrightarrow x_k\to x_\star.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Error-Bound Upgrade to Iterate Convergence

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,Ax_k)=0\) for every \(k\), but \((x_k)\) does not converge.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary maximal-monotone counterexample directly verifies the separation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A minimal separation between a vanishing inclusion residual and convergence of the underlying orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(x)=\{0\}\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R\), and define \(x_k=(-1)^k\). The operator \(A\) is maximal monotone and \(\operatorname{zer}A=\mathbb R\). Hence the natural inclusion residual satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(0,Ax_k)=0\) for every \(k\), although \((x_k)\) alternates between \(-1\) and \(1\) and therefore has no limit. Thus residual decay, even exact residual vanishing, does not by itself certify iterate convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the zero maximal monotone operator, an alternating sequence has zero residual at every step but does not converge.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Decay without Iterate Convergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-operator counterexample correctly separates residual vanishing from iterate convergence, but no source is supplied.

children.title: Infinite-Dimensional Geometric Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Weak-only convergence and failures of Hilbertian arguments.

children.title: Infinite-Dimensional Compactness Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by the absence of finite-dimensional compactness mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Sequential Compactness of Bounded Hilbert Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The surviving weak compactness mechanism contrasted with failure of norm precompactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space. Every bounded sequence \((x_n)\subset H\) has a weakly convergent subsequence. Thus the closed unit ball is weakly sequentially compact, although in infinite dimension it need not be norm sequentially compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded Hilbert-space sequences have weakly convergent subsequences, even though boundedness does not provide norm-convergent subsequences in infinite dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists (x_{n_j})\text{ and }x\in H\text{ such that }x_{n_j}\rightharpoonup x.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Sequential Compactness of Bounded Hilbert Sequences

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closed unit ball of \(H\) is not sequentially compact in the norm topology.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm compactness available in finite dimensions fails for bounded sequences in infinite-dimensional Hilbert space.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(H=\ell^2\), the sequence \((e_n)\) lies in the closed unit ball \(B_H\). For distinct indices \(m\neq n\), one has \(\|e_m-e_n\|=\sqrt{2}\). Consequently, \((e_n)\) has no norm-Cauchy subsequence and hence no norm-convergent subsequence. Thus boundedness alone supplies no norm-precompactness in infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, so convergence arguments relying on extraction of strongly convergent subsequences require an additional compactness mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The orthonormal basis of ℓ² is bounded but has no norm-convergent subsequence, invalidating finite-dimensional compactness arguments.
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Dimensional Compactness Obstructions

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((e_n)\) be the canonical orthonormal basis of \(H=\ell^2\). For the closed convex set \(C=\{0\}\), the sequence is Fejér monotone because \(\|e_{n+1}-0\|=\|e_n-0\|=1\). Moreover, \(e_n\rightharpoonup0\), while \(\|e_n-0\|=1\) for every \(n\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive closure boundary complementing failure of weak-by-weak graph closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone. If \((x_n,u_n)\in\operatorname{gra}A\), \(x_n\to x\) in norm, and \(u_n\rightharpoonup u\), then \((x,u)\in\operatorname{gra}A\). The same conclusion holds if \(x_n\rightharpoonup x\) and \(u_n\to u\) in norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximal-monotone graph is closed when either coordinate converges strongly and the other weakly, although weak convergence in both coordinates can fail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_n\to x,\ u_n\rightharpoonup u\Rightarrow(x,u)\in\operatorname{gra}A\), and \(x_n\rightharpoonup x,\ u_n\to u\Rightarrow(x,u)\in\operatorname{gra}A\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The graph of a maximal monotone operator need not be sequentially closed for weak convergence in both coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak convergence in both graph coordinates is insufficient for maximal-monotone graph closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((e_n)\) be the canonical basis and set \(x_n=(e_1+e_n)/\sqrt{2}\) for \(n\geq2\). Since \(\|x_n\|=1\), choosing \(y_n=x_n\) gives \(y_n\in N_B(x_n)\). Both sequences converge weakly to \(x=y=e_1/\sqrt{2}\). However, \(\|x\|<1\), so \(N_B(x)=\{0\}\) and \(y\notin N_B(x)\). Therefore \(\operatorname{gra}N_B\) is not weak-by-weak sequentially closed, despite \(N_B\) being maximal monotone.

knowledge_statements.title: Variational-Inequality Algorithms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected fixed-point iteration for a Hilbert-space variational inequality, stated without an unsupported convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in C\), an iteration budget \(N\geq1\), and step sizes \(\gamma_k>0\), compute \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\gamma_kF(x_k))\) for \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\). Define \(r_k=\|x_k-P_C(x_k-\gamma_kF(x_k))\|\), choose \(\widehat k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\leq k<N}r_k\), and return \(x_{\widehat k}\) together with \(r_{\widehat k}\). For every fixed \(\gamma>0\), a point \(x^\star\in C\) satisfies \(\langle F(x^\star),y-x^\star\rangle\geq0\) for all \(y\in C\) if and only if \(x^\star=P_C(x^\star-\gamma F(x^\star))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected iteration returns the iterate with the smallest observed projection residual; a zero residual is exactly a variational-inequality solution.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a Hilbert space \(H\).
\(F:C\to H\) is available through point evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns an observed iterate and its projection residual, without asserting that the residual is small under the stated assumptions.

source_refs.source_title: An Introduction to Variational Inequalities and Their Applications
source_refs.locator: Chapter III. Variational Inequalities for Monotone Operators p. 83

source_witnesses.source_title: An Introduction to Variational Inequalities and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-projection method for monotone Lipschitz variational inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(x_0\in C\), choose \(0<\gamma<1/L\) and set \[y_k=P_C(x_k-\gamma F(x_k)),\qquad x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\gamma F(y_k)).\] If the VI solution set is nonempty, then \(x_k-y_k\to0\) and \(x_k\) converges weakly to a VI solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extragradient uses a predictive projection and a corrected projection and converges for monotone Lipschitz VIs.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\rightharpoonup x^\star\in\operatorname{SOL}(F,C).
knowledge_statements.title: Korpelevich Extragradient Method

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Rate of Projected Gradient Under Strong Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction regime for the accepted projected VI iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F\) is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone and \(L\)-Lipschitz, then \(T_\gamma=P_C(I-\gamma F)\) satisfies \[\|T_\gamma x-T_\gamma y\|\leq q\|x-y\|,\qquad q=\sqrt{1-2\gamma\mu+\gamma^2L^2}.\] Thus, for \(0<\gamma<2\mu/L^2\), the VI has a unique solution \(x^\star\) and \(\|x_k-x^\star\|\leq q^k\|x_0-x^\star\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity make projected gradient a contraction for sufficiently small steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x_k-x^\star\|\leq q^k\|x_0-x^\star\|\quad\text{with }0<q<1.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Rate of Projected Gradient Under Strong Monotonicity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon dual-gap rate on a bounded VI domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the extragradient iterates above, let \(\bar y_N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}y_k\). Then for every \(z\in C\), \[\langle F(z),\bar y_N-z\rangle\leq\frac{\|x_0-z\|^2}{2\gamma N}.\] If \(D_0=\sup_{z\in C}\|x_0-z\|<\infty\), the dual gap \(g_D(\bar y_N)=\sup_{z\in C}\langle F(z),\bar y_N-z\rangle\) satisfies \(g_D(\bar y_N)\leq D_0^2/(2\gamma N)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaged extragradient prediction points attain an inverse-iteration dual-gap bound on bounded domains.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of the Korpelevich extragradient record hold.
\(D_0=\sup_{z\in C}\|x_0-z\|<\infty\) for the uniform gap bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g_D(\bar y_N)\leq D_0^2/(2\gamma N).

notation.meaning: Average of the extragradient prediction points

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Gap Bound for Extragradient

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Forward Projection Can Fail for Monotone Lipschitz Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of stronger structure or a corrected step for the basic projected iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\mathbb R^2\) and \(F(x)=Sx\), where \(S=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\). Then \(F\) is monotone and 1-Lipschitz and has the unique zero \(0\), but \[x_{k+1}=(I-\gamma S)x_k,\qquad \|x_{k+1}\|=\sqrt{1+\gamma^2}\|x_k\|.\] Hence the one-step forward iteration diverges for every \(\gamma>0\) and every \(x_0\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity alone do not make one-step projected gradient convergent.
knowledge_statements.title: Forward Projection Can Fail for Monotone Lipschitz Maps

children.title: Complementarity Algorithms

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite complementary-pivot path method for linear complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the LCP \(w=Mz+q\), \(z\geq0\), \(w\geq0\), and \(z^Tw=0\), Lemke's method introduces an artificial variable and follows adjacent complementary bases. If \(M\) is a P-matrix and degeneracy is handled by a lexicographic anti-cycling rule, the path terminates after finitely many pivots at the unique LCP solution rather than on a secondary ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a P-matrix LCP, Lemke's complementary-pivot path terminates finitely at the unique solution.
assumptions_latex: Degeneracy is handled by a lexicographic or equivalent anti-cycling rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Lemke's path terminates at the unique complementary pair }(z,w).

notation.meaning: Matrix whose principal minors are all positive

knowledge_statements.title: Lemke Algorithm for P-Matrix LCPs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the seed projected iteration under mere evaluability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n=1\), \(F(x)=1-x\), \(x_0=2\), and \(\gamma=1\), the projected iteration is \[x_{k+1}=\max\{0,2x_k-1\}.\] Hence \(x_k=1+2^k\) and the iterates diverge, although the nonlinear complementarity problem has the solution \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact natural-residual identity does not by itself make projected complementarity iteration convergent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k=1+2^k\to\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Complementarity Iteration Needs Regularity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Short-Step Primal–Dual Path Following for Monotone LCPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central-path method for a strictly feasible monotone linear complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w=Mz+q\), maintain \(z>0\), \(w>0\), \(\mu=z^Tw/n\), and \(\|ZWe-\mu e\|_2\leq\theta\mu\). There exist universal short-step constants \(\theta,c,c'>0\) such that, with \(\sigma=1-c/\sqrt n\), the Newton system \[M\Delta z-\Delta w=0,\qquad W\Delta z+Z\Delta w=\sigma\mu e-ZWe\] has a full step that remains in the neighborhood and satisfies \(\mu^+\leq(1-c'/\sqrt n)\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A short-step primal–dual Newton method follows the central path of a strictly feasible monotone LCP and geometrically decreases complementarity.
assumptions_latex: A strictly feasible initial pair satisfies \(w_0=Mz_0+q\), \(z_0>0\), \(w_0>0\), and belongs to the stated neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((z_k,w_k)\) remains strictly feasible and \(\mu_{k+1}\leq(1-c'/\sqrt n)\mu_k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Short-Step Primal–Dual Path Following for Monotone LCPs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial Complexity of Short-Step Monotone-LCP Path Following
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration complexity measured by the primal–dual complementarity gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mu_{k+1}\leq(1-c/\sqrt n)\mu_k\) for a universal \(c>0\), then \[k\geq C\sqrt n\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon)\] iterations suffice for \(z_k^Tw_k=n\mu_k\leq n\varepsilon\), for a universal \(C>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Short-step path following reaches a prescribed complementarity gap in order square-root-of-dimension times a logarithmic accuracy factor.
assumptions_latex: The hypotheses and neighborhood invariance of the short-step monotone-LCP method hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k=O\!\left(\sqrt n\log\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right)\Longrightarrow z_k^Tw_k\leq n\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Complexity of Short-Step Monotone-LCP Path Following

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A zero projection residual certifies \(x\geq0\), \(F(x)\geq0\), and \(x_iF_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orthant projection identity gives the componentwise complementarity equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected natural-residual algorithm for a nonlinear complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb R_+^n\), tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and steps \(\gamma_k>0\), set \(x_{k+1}=P_+(x_k-\gamma_kF(x_k))\). Stop when \(\|r_{\gamma_k}(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\), where \(r_\gamma(x)=x-P_+(x-\gamma F(x))\), and return \(x_k\). For every \(\gamma>0\), \(r_\gamma(x)=0\) is equivalent to the nonlinear complementarity conditions \(x\geq0\), \(F(x)\geq0\), and \(x_iF_i(x)=0\) for all \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto the nonnegative orthant yields an iteration whose zero residual is exactly the nonlinear complementarity condition.

assumptions_latex: The nonlinear complementarity problem uses componentwise inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complementarity problem is equivalent to the square equation \(\Phi(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fischer-Burmeister reduction of finite-dimensional complementarity to a nonsmooth equation.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 9. Equation-Based Algorithms for CPs p. 793
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\phi(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}-a-b\) and \(\Phi_i(x)=\phi(x_i,F_i(x))\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\). The scalar equivalence \(\phi(a,b)=0\) if and only if \(a\geq0\), \(b\geq0\), and \(ab=0\) yields \[\Phi(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\geq0,\quad F(x)\geq0,\quad x_iF_i(x)=0\ \text{for all }i.\] Thus a complementarity problem can be passed to a nonsmooth equation solver without changing its solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fischer-Burmeister map converts componentwise complementarity exactly into a square system of nonsmooth equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Equation-Reduction Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 9. Equation-Based Algorithms for CPs p. 793
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise-smooth NCP-function reduction complementary to the accepted Fischer–Burmeister seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(M_i(x)=\min\{x_i,F_i(x)\}\). Then \[M(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\geq0,\quad F(x)\geq0,\quad x_iF_i(x)=0\ \text{for all }i.\] Thus the componentwise minimum map and the Fischer–Burmeister map have the same zero set, although their generalized derivatives need not coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The componentwise minimum map is a second exact nonsmooth equation reduction of the nonlinear complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M^{-1}(0)=\operatorname{SOL}(\operatorname{NCP}(F)).
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Map Complementarity Equation
