children.title: Primal–Dual Splitting
children.top_down_role: Transfer to splitting methods organized around coupled primal and dual variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic PDHG rate for the convex composite saddle problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y)\). Run the seed PDHG iteration with \(\theta=1\), constant steps satisfying \(\tau\sigma\|K\|^2<1\), and define \(x^N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N x_k\) and \(y^N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N y_k\). Then, for every testing pair \((x,y)\), \[L(x^N,y)-L(x,y^N)\leq \frac{\|x-x_0\|^2}{2\tau N}+\frac{\|y-y_0\|^2}{2\sigma N}.\] Supremizing over bounded testing sets gives an \(O(N^{-1})\) restricted primal–dual gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ergodic PDHG averages satisfy an inverse-iteration restricted saddle-gap bound.
assumptions_latex: The composite saddle problem has a saddle point.
The seed PDHG iteration uses \(\theta=1\), constant \(\tau,\sigma>0\), and \(\tau\sigma\|K\|^2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(x^N,y)-L(x,y^N)=O(N^{-1})\text{ for each fixed testing pair }(x,y).
knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Primal–Dual Gap Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite Saddle, KKT, and Fenchel-Dual Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local primal–dual formulation targeted by PDHG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x f(x)+g(Kx)\), define \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y)\). A pair \((x^\star,y^\star)\) is a saddle point exactly when \[0\in\partial f(x^\star)+K^*y^\star,\qquad 0\in\partial g^*(y^\star)-Kx^\star.\] Under \(0\in\operatorname{sri}(K\operatorname{dom}f-\operatorname{dom}g)\), the associated primal and Fenchel dual \(\sup_y[-f^*(-K^*y)-g^*(y)]\) have zero duality gap whenever an optimal pair exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PDHG targets the saddle/KKT system associated with the composite primal problem and its Fenchel dual.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Hilbert spaces, \(K:X\to Y\) is bounded linear, and \(f,g\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^\star,y^\star)\text{ is a saddle pair if and only if it satisfies the displayed KKT inclusions.}
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Saddle, KKT, and Fenchel-Dual Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability of the scalar basic PDHG recurrence beyond its exact linear stability threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=Y=\mathbb R\), \(K=I\), \(f=g^*=0\), and \(\theta=1\), put \(a=\tau\sigma\). Eliminating the dual iterate gives \[x_{k+1}=2(1-a)x_k-(1-a)x_{k-1}.\] If \(a>4/3\), its characteristic polynomial has a root of modulus greater than one, so suitable initial data produce unbounded iterates. At \(a=4/3\), the root \(-1\) prevents convergence for generic initial data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scalar bilinear PDHG recurrence becomes unstable once the product of the steps exceeds four thirds; the standard condition below one is sufficient but not the exact scalar stability threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau\sigma>4/3\Longrightarrow\exists(x_0,y_0)\text{ for which }\|(x_k,y_k)\|\to\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Bilinear Step-Size Instability Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed variable-metric primal–dual splitting with a positive block coupling metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:X\to X\) and \(\Sigma:Y\to Y\) be bounded, self-adjoint, strongly positive operators satisfying
\[\|\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\|<1.\]
With \(\operatorname{prox}^{T^{-1}}_f=(I+T\partial f)^{-1}\) and \(\operatorname{prox}^{\Sigma^{-1}}_{g^*}=(I+\Sigma\partial g^*)^{-1}\), iterate
\[y_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{\Sigma^{-1}}_{g^*}(y_k+\Sigma K\bar x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{T^{-1}}_f(x_k-TK^*y_{k+1}),\]
\[\bar x_{k+1}=2x_{k+1}-x_k.\]
If a saddle point exists, the iterates converge weakly to a saddle point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive primal and dual metrics give a convergent preconditioned PDHG method when the scaled coupling norm is below one.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and \(\Sigma\) are bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_k,y_k)\) converges weakly to a saddle point.
knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned PDHG

knowledge_statements.scope_note: PDHG acceleration when the primal term is strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(f\) is \(\gamma\)-strongly convex. Starting with \(\tau_0\sigma_0\|K\|^2<1\), perform the PDHG proximal updates and set
\[\theta_k=(1+2\gamma\tau_k)^{-1/2},\qquad \tau_{k+1}=\theta_k\tau_k,\qquad \sigma_{k+1}=\sigma_k/\theta_k,\]
\[\bar x_{k+1}=x_{k+1}+\theta_k(x_{k+1}-x_k).\]
For every saddle point \((x^\star,y^\star)\), \(\|x_k-x^\star\|^2=O(k^{-2})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity permits reciprocal step updates yielding an order-one-over-k-squared bound for squared primal distance.
assumptions_latex: The composite saddle problem has a saddle point.

notation.meaning: strong-convexity modulus of the primal term

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Accelerated PDHG
Primal–Dual Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-budget primal–dual hybrid gradient splitting for a composite convex problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in X\), \(y_0\in Y\), and \(\bar x_0=x_0\). For \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), compute \[y_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y_k+\sigma K\bar x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x_k-\tau K^*y_{k+1}),\] followed by \(\bar x_{k+1}=x_{k+1}+\theta(x_{k+1}-x_k)\). Return \((x_N,y_N)\). Any fixed point with \(\bar x=x\) satisfies \(0\in\partial f(x)+K^*y\) and \(0\in\partial g^*(y)-Kx\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method performs a fixed number of alternating primal and dual proximal updates; every fixed point satisfies the composite saddle-point inclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Hilbert spaces, \(K:X\to Y\) is bounded linear, and \(f,g\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is a primal–dual splitting scheme, and each of its fixed points satisfies the stated saddle-point inclusion.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard primal-dual hybrid gradient update stated with its step-size condition

children.title: Stochastic Splitting
children.top_down_role: Transfer to splitting methods with stochastic evaluations or sampling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of last-iterate convergence with constant steps and nonsummable noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take \(H=\mathbb R\), \(A=B=0\), constant \(\gamma>0\), and independent Rademacher errors \(\xi_k\). Then \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\gamma\xi_k\) is a symmetric random walk and does not converge almost surely, although the oracle is conditionally unbiased and has uniformly bounded variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbiased bounded-variance noise alone does not ensure convergence with a constant step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb P((x_k)\text{ converges})=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Noise Failure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-Sure Convergence of Stochastic Forward–Backward Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-step stochastic forward–backward splitting with summable conditional noise energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[x_{k+1}=J_{\gamma A}\bigl(x_k-\gamma(Bx_k+\xi_k)\bigr),\qquad 0<\gamma<2\beta.\] If \(\mathbb E[\xi_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\) and \(\sum_k\mathbb E[\|\xi_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]<\infty\) almost surely, then the iterates are stochastic quasi-Fejér with respect to \(\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\) and converge weakly almost surely to a random point in that set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cocoercive forward operator and summable conditional noise energy give almost-sure weak convergence of stochastic forward–backward splitting.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximally monotone and \(B\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive on a Hilbert space.
The errors are adapted, conditionally unbiased, and have almost-surely summable conditional second moments.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Douglas–Rachford Residual Certifies Consensus Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound one-way certificate and exact fixed-point characterization for a product-space Douglas–Rachford step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma F}(z)\) and \(y=P_D(2x-z)\). Then \[y=x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in D\ \text{ and }\ x-z\in N_D(x).\] Since \(z-x\in\gamma\partial F(x)\), either equivalent condition implies \(0\in\partial F(x)+N_D(x)\). Thus a zero Douglas–Rachford update residual certifies that the common component of \(x\) minimizes \(\sum_i f_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero distributed Douglas–Rachford residual exactly characterizes a fixed point and certifies consensus optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y=x\iff[x\in D\text{ and }x-z\in N_D(x)]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad0\in\partial F(x)+N_D(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Douglas–Rachford Residual Certifies Consensus Optimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact Communication Requires Quantitative Error Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the exact-consensus-projection Douglas–Rachford formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the communication step is replaced by \[y_k=P_D(2x_k-z_k)+e_k\] with uncontrolled errors \(e_k\), the iteration is no longer the exact Douglas–Rachford fixed-point iteration, and convergence to a consensual solution is not guaranteed. Standard perturbation guarantees require quantitative control such as summability of \(\|e_k\|\), or a jointly contractive communication process analyzed together with the optimization dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary averaging errors can destroy distributed Douglas–Rachford convergence; the errors must be quantitatively controlled.
assumptions_latex: \text{No decay, summability, or coupled contraction assumption is imposed on }e_k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Convergence and consensus are not guaranteed without quantitative control of }e_k.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Communication Requires Quantitative Error Control

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed convex minimization in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be finite dimensional, let \(f_i\in\Gamma_0(H)\), define \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)\), and let \(D=\{(x_i):x_1=\cdots=x_m\}\). Suppose \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}F)\cap D\ne\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}\sum_i f_i(x)\ne\varnothing\). For the product-space Douglas–Rachford iteration in the immutable seed, assume \(\lambda_k\in[\varepsilon,2-\varepsilon]\) for some \(\varepsilon>0\). Then \(z_k\) converges to a Douglas–Rachford fixed point, \(x_k-y_k\to0\), and \(x_k\) and \(y_k\) converge to a consensual product vector whose common component minimizes \(\sum_i f_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact averaging, a standard qualification, and relaxation bounded away from zero and two, product-space distributed Douglas–Rachford converges to a consensus minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_k\to z_\star,\qquad x_k-y_k\to0,\qquad x_k,y_k\to(\bar x,\ldots,\bar x),\qquad \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}\sum_i f_i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space Douglas-Rachford interface for distributed convex minimization with exact averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(z_0=(z_{1,0},\ldots,z_{m,0})\in H^m\). At iteration \(k\), every agent computes \(x_{i,k}=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_i}(z_{i,k})\). Communication then evaluates \(y_k=P_D(2x_k-z_k)\), equivalently setting every component of \(y_k\) to the average of the components of \(2x_k-z_k\). Update \[z_{k+1}=z_k+\lambda_k(y_k-x_k).\] Stop when \(\|y_k-x_k\|\leq\varepsilon\), and return the common value represented by \(P_Dx_k\). This is Douglas-Rachford splitting for \(0\in\partial F+N_D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Product-space Douglas-Rachford uses local proximal steps and an averaging communication step to enforce consensus among agents.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Connectivity without Aperiodicity Need Not Contract
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp aperiodicity boundary for consensus mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(W=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\), the communication graph is connected and \(W\) is doubly stochastic, but \(W^k\) alternates between \(I\) and \(W\). Thus disagreement is not contracted and the iterates need not converge to consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A connected two-agent swap matrix oscillates forever, showing why consensus mixing requires aperiodicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W^k\not\to\tfrac12\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top.
knowledge_statements.title: Connectivity without Aperiodicity Need Not Contract

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Row-Stochastic Mixing Does Not Preserve the Arithmetic Average
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating consensus from average consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every \(W_k\) is only row stochastic, then \(W_k\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) preserves the consensus subspace, but generally \(\mathbf1^\top W_k\ne\mathbf1^\top\), so the arithmetic average is not invariant. Even when products converge to consensus, their limit may be a nonuniform weighted average unless balance, column stochasticity, or a push-sum correction is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row-stochastic communication may reach consensus without reaching the arithmetic average.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Consensus does not imply preservation of }m^{-1}\mathbf1^\top z.
knowledge_statements.title: Row-Stochastic Mixing Does Not Preserve the Arithmetic Average

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral contraction for a fixed undirected mixing matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be symmetric and doubly stochastic, with a connected graph, and suppose \(W\) is aperiodic. Set \(J=m^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\) and \(\rho=\max_{i\ge2}|\lambda_i(W)|\). Then \(\rho<1\) and \[\|W^k-J\|_2=\rho^k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A connected aperiodic symmetric mixing matrix preserves averages and contracts Euclidean disagreement at its subdominant spectral radius.
assumptions_latex: \text{The communication graph is connected and }W\text{ is aperiodic}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|W^k-J\|_2=\rho^k\quad\text{with }\rho<1.

Communication-Model Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A jointly connected, uniformly positive, aperiodic communication model ensuring multi-round disagreement contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\geq2\). For every \(k\), let \(W_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonnegative and doubly stochastic, satisfy \((W_k)_{ii}\geq\alpha\) for every \(i\), and have every positive entry at least \(\alpha>0\). Assume that, for some \(L\geq1\), the union of the directed communication graphs from rounds \(k\) through \(k+L-1\) is strongly connected for every \(k\). For \(z\in\mathbb R^m\), define \(\delta(z)=\max_i z_i-\min_i z_i\). Then there exist an integer \(s\geq L\) and \(q\in(0,1)\), depending only on \(m,L,\alpha\), such that \[\delta(W_{k+s-1}\cdots W_kz)\leq q\,\delta(z)\] for every \(k\) and every \(z\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive self-weights, doubly stochastic mixing, and repeated joint strong connectivity ensure uniform multi-round contraction of disagreement.
assumptions_latex: \(m\geq2\), and each \(W_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonnegative and doubly stochastic.
There is \(\alpha>0\) such that every diagonal entry and every other positive entry of every \(W_k\) is at least \(\alpha\).
For some \(L\geq1\), every union of \(L\) consecutive communication graphs is strongly connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(s\geq L\) and \(q\in(0,1)\) such that every product of \(s\) consecutive mixing matrices contracts the disagreement seminorm by at least the factor \(q\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic value-oracle lower bound for Lipschitz monotone variational inequalities on a Euclidean ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, for every \(N\), every deterministic value-oracle method making at most \(N\) adaptive queries, and sufficiently large dimension, one can choose a monotone \(L\)-Lipschitz mapping \(F:Q\to\mathbb{R}^d\) for which the method's output \(x_N\in Q\) satisfies
\[
g_F(x_N)=\sup_{u\in Q}\langle F(u),x_N-u\rangle\geq \frac{cLR^2}{N+1}.
\]
Consequently, a uniform guarantee \(g_F(x_N)\leq\varepsilon\) requires \(N+1\geq cLR^2/\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any deterministic value-oracle method needs on the order of LR squared over epsilon queries to solve every Lipschitz monotone variational inequality to dual-gap accuracy epsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Lower Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and leaf placement fit, but the specific deterministic oracle lower bound, gap convention, universal constant, and required dimension depend on the oracle model and need a directly supporting theorem-level citation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificate for a finite conic performance-estimation relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a valid finite performance-estimation relaxation be \[p^\star=\sup\{c^Tz:Az=b,\ z\in\mathcal K\},\] with dual \[d^\star=\inf\{b^Ty:A^Ty-c\in\mathcal K^*\}.\] Every dual-feasible \(y\) certifies \(p^\star\leq b^Ty\), and therefore certifies the same uniform upper bound for the terminal performance measure represented by the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible dual point of a valid conic performance-estimation relaxation provides a checkable worst-case upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K\) is a convex cone and the displayed conic relaxation is valid for every admissible oracle transcript.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A^Ty-c\in\mathcal K^*\Longrightarrow p^\star\leq b^Ty.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Feasible Performance Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Relaxation Gap from Omitting Lipschitz Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-point transcript separating a monotonicity-only relaxation from a monotone Lipschitz class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x_1=0\), \(g_1=0\), \(x_2=1\), and \(C=(g_2-g_1)^2\). For scalar monotone \(L\)-Lipschitz maps, realizability forces \(|g_2-g_1|\le L\), hence \(C\le L^2\). A relaxation retaining only monotonicity requires merely \((g_2-g_1)(x_2-x_1)\ge0\), so every \(g_2=M\ge0\) is feasible and its relaxed value is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping Lipschitz interpolation admits arbitrarily steep monotone transcripts that no map in the stated operator class can realize.
assumptions_latex: The realizable class consists of scalar monotone \(L\)-Lipschitz maps.
The relaxation enforces only pairwise monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\mathrm{realizable}}C\le L^2<+\infty=\sup_{\mathrm{relaxed}}C\).

notation.meaning: squared oracle-value difference used as performance measure

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Relaxation Gap from Omitting Lipschitz Interpolation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Gram-Matrix SDP for Cocoercive Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-transcript performance estimation for a single-valued cocoercive operator class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite set of pairs \((x_i,g_i)\) is interpolable by a \(\beta\)-cocoercive mapping on a Hilbert space if and only if
\[\langle g_i-g_j,x_i-x_j\rangle\ge\beta\|g_i-g_j\|^2\qquad\text{for all }i,j.\]
If an algorithm's updates are linear in the stored \(x_i,g_i\) and its performance measure is quadratic in them, the interpolation inequalities, update relations, initial conditions, and objective become linear in a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix. The resulting finite SDP is exact for this operator class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Necessary-and-sufficient cocoercive interpolation converts a quadratic finite-transcript worst-case problem exactly into a Gram-matrix semidefinite program.
assumptions_latex: The operator class consists of single-valued \(\beta\)-cocoercive mappings on a Hilbert space.
Only finitely many oracle pairs are used.
Algorithm relations are linear and the performance measure is quadratic in transcript vectors.
The ambient dimension is unrestricted, or the Gram formulation includes the required rank constraint for a fixed finite dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transcript worst-case value equals the optimum of the resulting Gram-matrix formulation.

notation.meaning: Gram matrix of the transcript vectors

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Gram-Matrix SDP for Cocoercive Interpolation

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{F}\) is a specified class of monotone operators on a common domain \(Q\).
The algorithm is described by oracle relations linking \(x_i\), \(F(x_i)\), and its internal states.
\(C\) is a prescribed terminal performance certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact worst-case certificate equals the supremum of \(C\) over all realizable finite oracle transcripts satisfying the class and algorithm constraints.

notation.meaning: Operator values returned at queried points
Set of realizable length-N oracle transcripts

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-based performance-estimation representation before any interpolation or semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal{T}_N\) contain precisely the tuples \((F,x_0,y_0,\ldots,x_N,y_N)\) such that \(F\in\mathcal{F}\), \(x_i\in Q\), \(y_i=F(x_i)\), and every update relation imposed by the algorithm holds. The worst-case value of the terminal certificate has the exact representation
\[
\mathcal{W}_N=\sup\left\{C(x_N,F):(F,x_0,y_0,\ldots,x_N,y_N)\in\mathcal{T}_N\right\}.
\]
Replacing realizability by necessary interpolation inequalities yields an upper-bounding finite performance-estimation problem; it is exact whenever those interpolation inequalities are also sufficient for membership in \(\mathcal{F}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Performance estimation maximizes the terminal certificate over every operator and oracle transcript consistent with the operator class and algorithm; exact interpolation conditions yield an exact finite reformulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Performance Estimation

children.title: Worst-Case Certificate Transfer
children.top_down_role: Connections between monotone residual certificates and worst-case complexity measures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise certificate conversions with unbounded instance constants do not imply a uniform rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the instance class contain \(I_m\) for all \(m\geq1\), and for each horizon \(N\geq1\) set \[C_N(I_m)=N^{-1},\qquad E_N(I_m)=\min\{1,m/N\},\qquad \psi_m(t)=mt.\] Then \(E_N(I_m)\leq\psi_m(C_N(I_m))\) for every fixed instance, while \(\sup_m C_N(I_m)=N^{-1}\to0\) and \(\sup_m E_N(I_m)=1\) for every \(N\). Thus pointwise conversions whose constants are unbounded over the instance class do not transfer a worst-case convergence rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Instancewise certificate bounds do not yield a worst-case rate unless the conversion is uniform across instances.
assumptions_latex: The instance class contains \(I_m\) for every positive integer \(m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_m C_N(I_m)\to0\quad\text{but}\quad\sup_m E_N(I_m)=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniformity Requirement for Worst-Case Transfer

assumptions_latex: For every admissible instance, the target error \(E_N\) and certificate \(C_N\) satisfy \(E_N\leq\psi(C_N)\).
A uniform certificate bound \(C_N\leq b_N\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup E_N\leq\psi(b_N)\) over the same instance class.

notation.meaning: Target worst-case error after N oracle calls or iterations
Verifiable convergence certificate after N calls or iterations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract transfer of a uniform certificate estimate into a worst-case error estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal{I}\) be an instance class. Suppose each \(I\in\mathcal{I}\) produces nonnegative quantities \(C_N(I)\) and \(E_N(I)\) satisfying \(E_N(I)\leq\psi(C_N(I))\), where \(\psi\) is nondecreasing. If performance estimation, an analytic argument, or an oracle bound establishes \(C_N(I)\leq b_N\) uniformly for all \(I\in\mathcal{I}\), then
\[
\sup_{I\in\mathcal{I}}E_N(I)\leq\sup_{I\in\mathcal{I}}\psi(C_N(I))\leq\psi(b_N).
\]
Thus the certificate rate transfers without changing the instance class, provided the conversion inequality is itself uniform.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform certificate bound transfers to a worst-case error bound whenever a nondecreasing, instance-uniform conversion controls error by the certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Certificate Transfer

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Differentiation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-normal and limiting-subdifferential definitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X^*\) be the dual of \(X\). The limiting normal cone to \(C\) at \(\bar x\) is
\[
N_C(\bar x)=\operatorname*{Limsup}_{x\to\bar x,\,x\in C}\widehat N_C(x),
\]
where
\[
\widehat N_C(x)=\left\{x^*\in X^*:\limsup_{u\to x,\,u\in C,\,u\ne x}\frac{\langle x^*,u-x\rangle}{\lVert u-x\rVert}\leq 0\right\}.
\]
With \(\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,r)\in X\times\mathbb{R}:r\geq f(x)\}\), the limiting subdifferential of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) is
\[
\partial f(\bar x)=\left\{x^*\in X^*:(x^*,-1)\in N_{\operatorname{epi}f}(\bar x,f(\bar x))\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The limiting normal cone is the outer limit of nearby Fréchet normal cones. The limiting subdifferential consists of dual vectors whose pairing with minus one is a limiting normal to the function's epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional normed space with dual \(X^*\).
\(C\subset X\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\in C\).
\(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x\), with \(f(\bar x)\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C(\bar x)\subset X^*\) and \(\partial f(\bar x)\subset X^*\) are respectively the limiting normal cone and limiting subdifferential defined above.

notation.meaning: Continuous dual of the finite-dimensional normed space X
Fréchet normal cone to C at x
Epigraph of f in the product space X times the real line

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a lower-semicontinuous function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) finite at \(\bar x\), define \[\widehat\partial f(\bar x):=\left\{x^*: \liminf_{x\to\bar x,\,x\ne\bar x}\frac{f(x)-f(\bar x)-\langle x^*,x-\bar x\rangle}{\|x-\bar x\|}\ge0\right\},\] and \[\partial^\infty f(\bar x):=\{x^*:(x^*,0)\in N_{\operatorname{epi}f}(\bar x,f(\bar x))\}.\] If \(f\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), then \(\partial^\infty f(\bar x)=\{0\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If the limiting normal cones satisfy the qualification
\[
N_A(\bar x)\cap\bigl(-N_B(\bar x)\bigr)=\{0\},
\]
then the limiting normal cone to the intersection obeys the calculus inclusion
\[
N_{A\cap B}(\bar x)\subset N_A(\bar x)+N_B(\bar x).
\]
Equivalently, every \(x^*\in N_{A\cap B}(\bar x)\) admits a decomposition \(x^*=a^*+b^*\) with \(a^*\in N_A(\bar x)\) and \(b^*\in N_B(\bar x)\). The qualification excludes nonzero opposing normals that obstruct this decomposition rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the basic no-opposing-normals qualification, every limiting normal to an intersection decomposes into limiting normals to the two constituent sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sum rule for lower-semicontinuous functions finite at the reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x\) and finite at \(\bar x\). If \[\partial^\infty f(\bar x)\cap[-\partial^\infty g(\bar x)]=\{0\},\] then \[\partial(f+g)(\bar x)\subset \partial f(\bar x)+\partial g(\bar x).\] The qualification holds in particular when one summand is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the singular-subgradient qualification, each limiting subgradient of a sum decomposes into limiting subgradients of its summands.
assumptions_latex: f,g\text{ are lower semicontinuous near }\bar x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial(f+g)(\bar x)\subset\partial f(\bar x)+\partial g(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.title: Qualified Limiting-Subdifferential Sum Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-subdifferential chain rule for a smooth inner mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be strictly differentiable at \(\bar x\), and let \(\varphi:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be lower semicontinuous near \(F(\bar x)\) and finite there. If \[\partial^\infty\varphi(F(\bar x))\cap\ker \nabla F(\bar x)^*=\{0\},\] then \[\partial(\varphi\circ F)(\bar x)\subset \nabla F(\bar x)^*\partial\varphi(F(\bar x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A qualified chain rule pulls outer limiting subgradients back through the adjoint derivative of the smooth inner map.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is strictly differentiable at }\bar x.
\varphi\text{ is lower semicontinuous near }F(\bar x)\text{ and finite there}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial(\varphi\circ F)(\bar x)\subset\nabla F(\bar x)^*\partial\varphi(F(\bar x)).
knowledge_statements.title: Qualified Smooth-Inner Chain Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional failure of the limiting-normal intersection inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A=\{(u,v):v\ge u^2\}\) and \(B=\{(u,v):v\le0\}\). Then \(A\cap B=\{(0,0)\}\), so \(N_{A\cap B}(0,0)=\mathbb R^2\), whereas
\[N_A(0,0)=\{(0,t):t\le0\},\qquad N_B(0,0)=\{(0,t):t\ge0\}.\]
Thus \(N_A(0,0)+N_B(0,0)=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\) does not contain \(N_{A\cap B}(0,0)\), and the no-opposing-normals qualification fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parabola epigraph and a lower half-space meet only at the origin, where the intersection normal is the whole plane but the sum of the constituent normals is only vertical.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{A\cap B}(0,0)\nsubseteq N_A(0,0)+N_B(0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Intersection Rule Failure Without Qualification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional maximum rule for locally Lipschitz functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), let \(f=\max_i f_i\), and let \(I(\bar x)=\{i:f_i(\bar x)=f(\bar x)\}\). Then
\[\partial f(\bar x)\subset\operatorname{co}\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}\partial f_i(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every limiting subgradient of a finite maximum lies in the convex hull of limiting subgradients of active functions.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial f(\bar x)\subset\operatorname{co}\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}\partial f_i(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Maximum Limiting-Subdifferential Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional marginal rule with localized minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu(x)=\inf_y\varphi(x,y)\) and \(M(x)=\operatorname{argmin}_y\varphi(x,y)\). Suppose \(\mu(\bar x)\) is finite, \(\varphi\) is lower semicontinuous near every \((\bar x,\bar y)\) with \(\bar y\in M(\bar x)\), and \(M\) is inner semicompact at \(\bar x\) relative to \(\operatorname{dom}\mu\). Then
\[\partial\mu(\bar x)\subset\bigcup_{\bar y\in M(\bar x)}\{x^*:(x^*,0)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A limiting subgradient of a marginal value is obtained from a joint limiting subgradient having zero component in a localized minimizing variable.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is lower semicontinuous near every relevant minimizing pair.
\(M\) is inner semicompact at \(\bar x\) relative to \(\operatorname{dom}\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial\mu(\bar x)\subset\bigcup_{\bar y\in M(\bar x)}\{x^*:(x^*,0)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)\}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative finite-dimensional refinement of the coderivative criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) have locally closed graph near \((\bar x,\bar y)\). If \(F\) has the Aubin property there, then \[\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\|D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\|^+:=\sup\{\|x^*\|:x^*\in D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*),\ \|y^*\|\le1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, the exact Aubin modulus equals the outer norm of the limiting coderivative.
assumptions_latex: F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\text{ has locally closed graph near }(\bar x,\bar y).
F\text{ has the Aubin property around }(\bar x,\bar y).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\|D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\|^+.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the limiting coderivative by
\[
D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)=\left\{x^*:(x^*,-y^*)\in N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\right\}.
\]
Then \(F\) has the Aubin property around \((\bar x,\bar y)\), meaning that some neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\), \(V\) of \(\bar y\), and some \(\ell\geq0\) satisfy
\[
F(x)\cap V\subset F(u)+\ell\|x-u\|\mathbb{B}\quad\text{for all }x,u\in U,
\]
if and only if
\[
D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(0)=\{0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally closed-graph multifunction is Lipschitz-like near a graph point exactly when its limiting coderivative sends the zero dual vector only to zero.
